If the directory is a Yocto build but holds neither an SPDX document nor an image manifest, the scan stops and names the two settings above rather than falling back to a directory scan whose result would misrepresent the image.

What you get differs from a normal SBOM scan in three ways.

The component list contains only the packages installed in the image. A Yocto document also describes every source archive the build consumed, which is useful for provenance but would misrepresent what the product ships. Those are left out.

Vulnerabilities come from the build itself. Yocto runs a CVE analysis while building and records a verdict per CVE, so it knows whether a recipe applied the patch. Those verdicts are shown split three ways: patched during the build, judged not applicable, and still open. Only the open ones are counted as findings. On the reference core-image-minimal image this is the difference between reporting 12255 vulnerabilities and reporting none, since every one of them was already closed by the build.

Components get the upstream repository purl, as in a firmware scan, for the projects BomLens can name from the build's records: by the recipe a package came from, or, for SPDX 2.2, by the recipe's source download address. See Upstream repository purl for which projects are covered.

Two limits are worth knowing before you start.

SPDX 2.2 is read, but with less in it. Yocto 4.0 (Kirkstone) and 5.0 (Scarthgap) emit SPDX 2.2 by default, and that form is not a document at all: the deploy directory holds one <image>.spdx.tar.zst and nothing else. Inside it are the image document, a document per installed package and one per recipe. BomLens reads the archive itself. Measured against the published Yocto 5.0.14 core-image-minimal, it yields the same 36 packages the image manifest lists, with their licenses and CPEs. What they do not give is the build's CVE verdicts (only SPDX 3.0 records which CVEs a recipe patched), so with --security vulnerabilities are matched from the CPEs against the NVD CPE index in the image (a CPE with vendor * by product name across every vendor, so a product name another project shares can bring that project's CVEs), and a CVE the build already patched can appear as open. Pull the image document out of the archive and upload it alone and you get an almost empty result, which is said rather than left to look like a clean scan. When a build directory holds both formats, the SPDX 3.0 document is the one analyzed even if the 2.2 one is newer. An archive passed to --analyze gets no conformance check report: it is a bundle of documents rather than a submitted one, so there is nothing to measure against the submission criteria. Found in a build directory, the SBOM read from it is checked instead.

Conformance checks that depend on PURL will fail. Yocto identifies packages with CPE rather than PURL, so PURL coverage and the checks derived from it cannot pass. The report says how many components carry a CPE instead, and the row cites the baselines — BSI TR-03183-2 and the US SBOM minimum elements — that accept either identifier. The verdict is the submission criteria's, not theirs: PURL is required here because the default vulnerability matching keys on it.

Two more required checks behave differently on a Yocto image, for reasons in the document rather than in the tool. The top-level component fails for want of a version: bitbake writes the image package with a name and no software_packageVersion (measured on the reference core-image-minimal). Scanned from a build directory, the image takes --version instead.

Uploads are capped at 100 MB. For scale, the reference core-image-minimal document is 15.8 MB with 35 installed packages. A build directory scanned with --target reads the file from disk, so the cap does not apply there.

docs.title: Asking for remediation
docs.text:
After validation and analysis, send the risk report (_risk-report.html) to whoever sent the SBOM and ask for the following.

  • Fix the conformance fail items and send the SBOM again.
  • Prepare a response plan or risk justification for Critical vulnerabilities within 7 days and High within 30 days (recommended deadlines).

Response tracking, exception approval, and history management are out of scope for this tool — they belong to a separate vulnerability and risk management system. This tool covers validating, analyzing, and reporting on a single SBOM locally.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Validation is based on the presence and coverage of required fields. It does not guarantee semantic accuracy such as whether a PURL points to the exact package or whether a version is real.
  • Whether transitive dependencies are included is inferred from the presence of edges in the dependency graph; it is not proof that the graph is complete.
  • The accuracy of vulnerability and license analysis depends directly on the quality of the input SBOM, especially PURL and version accuracy.

Related: Getting started | Scenarios guide | Notice and security guide | What the reports mean

docs.title: Upload to Dependency-Track / TRUSCA
docs.text:
This guide covers how the scanner uploads a generated SBOM and how to target TRUSCA's native ingest endpoint.

After a scan, the SBOM is uploaded by default (--generate-only saves locally and skips the upload). Choose the destination with UPLOAD_TARGET.

  • dependency-track (default): a regular Dependency-Track server. Authenticates with API_URL and API_KEY (X-Api-Key) and auto-creates the project.
  • trusca: TRUSCA's native ingest endpoint. It is not Dependency-Track compatible, so the auth and inputs differ.

To upload to TRUSCA, prepare three things.

  • API_URL: the TRUSCA server URL
  • API_KEY: a Bearer token issued by TRUSCA (starts with tos_, developer role)
  • project_id: the target TRUSCA project id (UUID). It must already exist; there is no auto-create.
API_URL="https://<TRUSCA host>" API_KEY="tos_..." \
  ./scripts/scan-sbom.sh \
  --project "MyApp" --version "1.2.3" --all \
  --trusca "<project_id>"

--trusca <id> is shorthand for --upload-target trusca plus TRUSCA_PROJECT_ID. Adjust the ref and release labels with TRUSCA_REF (default main) and TRUSCA_RELEASE (default the --version value). On acceptance it prints 202 and a scan id; track progress in the TRUSCA UI (GET /v1/scans/{id}).

TRUSCA ingest fills components, vulnerabilities, declared licenses, the dependency graph, and the build gate. It cannot fill scancode-detected licenses (--deep-license), the cosign signature (--sign), or source preservation, since there is no source tree. Generate those locally with --generate-only if you need them.

docs.title: From the web UI
docs.text: You can upload without the CLI. On the New scan form, turn on the Upload step, choose Dependency-Track or TRUSCA, and enter the server URL and access token (plus the project id for TRUSCA). The scan runs and then uploads in one step, using the same endpoints and authentication described above. The URL and token are used for that run only and are not saved. See the Web UI reference.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / fix TRUSCA upload needs API_URL, API_KEY (Bearer token), and TRUSCA_PROJECT_ID One of the three is missing. All three are required for --trusca / UPLOAD_TARGET=trusca; there is no partial mode. API_KEY and API_URL are required for upload Same requirement on the Dependency-Track path (the default target). Upload to <url> did not complete (curl exit N: no response) The server is unreachable — wrong URL, network/proxy, or the server is down. The scan itself already finished and its artifacts were saved; fix API_URL and re-upload, or add --generate-only to skip the upload step entirely. TRUSCA ingest failed (HTTP <code>) TRUSCA rejected the request. The response body printed alongside the error names the reason — a bad token, an unknown project id, or a malformed SBOM. Upload failed (HTTP <code>) (Dependency-Track) Same idea — the printed response body has the server's reason. A 401 usually means a wrong or expired API_KEY. Cannot reach Dependency Track at <url> (a warning, not a failure) A pre-flight check failed but the upload is attempted anyway, since some deployments block the version endpoint but still accept the BOM upload. If the upload itself then fails too, it is a real connectivity problem. Dependency-Track ... refused the CycloneDX 1.7 SBOM (HTTP 400) (a warning) Dependency-Track reads CycloneDX 1.7 from 4.14.4 and 5.1.0 on, and an older server refuses a 1.7 SBOM: one made with --spec-version 1.7, and an AI model or dataset SBOM (--model), which is 1.7 even at the default. When the server's /api/version names an older version, or names none, a 1.6 copy of the SBOM is sent once more; the saved SBOM stays 1.7. The copy also rewrites what 1.6 does not allow: a license list that mixes licenses and an expression becomes one expression joined with AND (or, when a license has no SPDX id, a list of licenses), and fields that only 1.7 has are removed. If the copy is refused too, both responses are printed. Dependency-Track <version> reads CycloneDX 1.7, so the refusal (HTTP 400) is not about the version (a warning) The server is 4.14.4 or later in 4.x, or 5.1.0 or later, and reads the 1.7 SBOM (--spec-version 1.7 or --model), so no 1.6 copy is sent. The printed response body has the server's reason.

For TRUSCA, HTTP 202 only means the ingest was queued; tracking it to completion happens in the TRUSCA UI (GET /v1/scans/{id}), not in BomLens.

Related: CLI reference | Web UI reference | Generate notice, security & risk reports

docs.title: Verify a release
docs.text:
A tool that reports on supply chains should have a supply chain you can check. Every release is built by the project's own GitHub Actions workflows and signed with keyless cosign (Sigstore), so you can confirm that what you downloaded was built from this repository, without trusting a key that someone could hand you.

The commands below were run against v1.13.7. Replace the version with the one you downloaded. They need cosign v2 and, for the checksum step, sha256sum (shasum -a 256 on macOS).

docs.title: Release files (installers, CLI, source bundles)
docs.text:
One signature covers the checksum file, and the checksum file covers every asset, so you verify one file and then the checksums.

VERSION=v1.13.7
gh release download "$VERSION" --repo sktelecom/bomlens \
  --pattern 'SHA256SUMS.txt*' --pattern 'BomLens-Setup.exe'

cosign verify-blob SHA256SUMS.txt \
  --signature SHA256SUMS.txt.sig \
  --certificate SHA256SUMS.txt.pem \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/sktelecom/bomlens/' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
# Verified OK

sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing
# BomLens-Setup.exe: OK

Verified OK means the checksum file was signed by a workflow of the sktelecom/bomlens repository. The OK line then says your file matches the checksum in it. The desktop installers are not code-signed yet (the first run shows a SmartScreen or Gatekeeper warning, see first scan); this check is how you confirm one is the project's build.

docs.title: On Windows
docs.text:
You need no gh, sha256sum or jq for this check. Download cosign-windows-amd64 from the cosign releases page into the folder you work in, rename it to cosign.exe, then run this in PowerShell. It downloads the installer and its checksum files, verifies the signature on the checksum file, and compares the installer's hash with the one listed.

$v = "v1.13.7"
$base = "https://github.com/sktelecom/bomlens/releases/download/$v"
foreach ($f in "SHA256SUMS.txt","SHA256SUMS.txt.sig","SHA256SUMS.txt.pem","BomLens-Setup.exe") {
  Invoke-WebRequest "$base/$f" -OutFile $f
}

.\cosign.exe verify-blob SHA256SUMS.txt `
  --signature SHA256SUMS.txt.sig `
  --certificate SHA256SUMS.txt.pem `
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/sktelecom/bomlens/' `
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
# Verified OK

$want = ((Select-String -Path SHA256SUMS.txt -Pattern 'BomLens-Setup.exe').Line -split '\s+')[0]
$got = (Get-FileHash BomLens-Setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
if ($want -ieq $got) { "OK: BomLens-Setup.exe matches" } else { "MISMATCH" }

If the last line prints MISMATCH, do not run the installer.

docs.title: Container image
docs.text:
The images are signed by digest, and each one carries its own SBOM as a signed attestation.

cosign verify ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens:1.13.7 \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/sktelecom/bomlens/' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com

To read the image's SBOM (CycloneDX) from the attestation:

cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens:1.13.7 \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/sktelecom/bomlens/' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  | head -1 | jq -r '.payload | @base64d | fromjson | .predicate' > bomlens-image.cdx.json

You can then run BomLens on its own image's SBOM: scan-sbom.sh --analyze bomlens-image.cdx.json --project bomlens-image --version 1.13.7.

docs.title: The project's own SBOM
docs.text: Each release also attaches bomlens-source-<version>.cdx.json, the SBOM of every manifest the repository ships (the desktop app's and the web UI's dependencies). It is covered by the same checksum file.

docs.title: What this does not tell you
docs.text: A valid signature says who built the file, not that the code is free of defects. The scanner image is scanned by Trivy every night and the findings are public in the repository's Security tab, and the limitations page lists what the tool does not do.

docs.title: Artifacts reference
docs.text:
The generated SBOM is CycloneDX 1.6 JSON, or 1.7 with --spec-version 1.7; AI model and dataset SBOMs are always 1.7. An SPDX 2.3 JSON copy, converted from the final CycloneDX BOM, is produced by --spdx during a CLI scan or on demand from the results screen in the UI. AI model and dataset scans also write an SPDX 3.0.1 document with the AI and Dataset profiles (_bom.spdx3.json, below). Both paths run the same conversion and give the same file. CycloneDX remains the primary format, and CycloneDX-only data (vulnerabilities, bomlens:* properties, and the services[] a declared AI service adds) is not carried over.

The filename is {Project}_{Version}_bom.json (e.g. MyApp_1.0.0_bom.json).

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
File When generated Description {Project}_{Version}_bom.json always SBOM (CycloneDX 1.6, or 1.7 with --spec-version 1.7) {Project}_{Version}_bom.refused.json a source scan or Yocto build directory scan whose declaration file (--components, or sbom-declared.cdx.json at the scan target root) is refused the SBOM written up to the point the scan stopped, without the declared components. It takes the place of _bom.json, which is not written, so a step that picks up _bom.json cannot take the incomplete SBOM; the scan prints the reasons and exits 1. Not normalized, signed or uploaded, and no report is made from it. The web UI's failed scan offers it to view or download. The next scan of the same project and version removes it. See What is refused, and why? {Project}_{Version}_bom.spdx.json --spdx / --all, or Export as SPDX 2.3 in the UI SBOM (SPDX 2.3, converted from the CycloneDX output) {Project}_{Version}_bom.spdx3.json AI model and dataset scans (--model, --model-file, a dataset), unless --no-spdx3 the AI SBOM as an SPDX 3.0.1 document with the AI and Dataset profiles (JSON-LD). Fields come from the CycloneDX output, from fixed rules over it, or from the publisher's declaration (--ai-declare); nothing is estimated. Required fields SPDX gives no "unknown" value (who supplied and who made the model and data, release and build dates, the download address, the document's author) stay empty until declared, and the document says it is a draft until then. Base models are identified by id and licence only. The weights scope is carried as bomlens:weights:scope (full, adapter, quantized, merged) in a CycloneDX properties extension. Not an input for --analyze {Project}_{Version}_spdx3-check.json / .md with the SPDX 3.0.1 document which field of each element came from the scan, from the declaration, or from nothing, which required fields are open, and what needs a decision by the publisher (personal data, safety risk, autonomy). service.state says whether the CycloneDX SBOM carries the declared service and model values: none (nothing declared, nothing in the SBOM), applied (the SBOM matches the declaration) or pendingScan (they differ; a new scan writes them). Guidance, not legal advice {Project}_{Version}_ai-declaration.template.json with the SPDX 3.0.1 document an empty declaration for this scan: the fields a person fills, for the model, its datasets and the base models the scan found. Fill it and pass it back with --ai-declare {Project}_{Version}_ai-declaration.json --ai-declare <file> (the accepted file), or the declaration saved in the web UI what the model's publisher declared. Like _vex.json, it is not removed by re-scanning the same project and version, and a re-scan applies it again. A file that names a dataset or base model the new scan does not have is refused, and the document stays a draft. A dataset entry can list sources[]: {"ref": "huggingface:<id>", "relation": "extended"} for a hub dataset (read from the hub at the next scan and judged with the dataset), or {"name": "...", "license": "<hub licence tag or SPDX id>", "relation": "other"} for one named in words (written to the SPDX 3.0.1 document only, marked as not verified; a licence that is not an SPDX id is kept in words). Data the hub does not hold takes sources named in words only. model.license (a hub licence tag or SPDX id) is the model's own licence: it fills the SPDX document when the scan read none or only other (as an SPDX expression only when it is a hub tag naming one SPDX licence, or a LicenseRef-), and a model described from the declaration alone carries it in its SBOM and is judged on it. A declaration can also describe the service the model runs in (service) and give the model's input and output kinds and regulatory values; see The declared AI service {Project}_{Version}_component-versions.template.csv a firmware, root filesystem or binary scan that found components without a version the names of those components in the --component-versions format (CSV with the header name,version,reason) with the versions left empty, and comment lines explaining the three reasons. A component that already carries a reason is not listed. Fill in a version, or a reason when there is none, and pass it back with --component-versions {Project}_{Version}_NOTICE.txt / .html --notice / --all / risk report default open-source notice {Project}_{Version}_NOTICE.pdf same as above, when a PDF renderer is built into the image (--build-arg SBOM_PDF=true) the notice rendered to PDF; skipped with a log line otherwise {Project}_{Version}_security.json / .md / .html --security / --all / risk report default Trivy security report {Project}_{Version}_risk-report.md / .html default (all modes) — omit with --no-report open-source risk report {Project}_{Version}_conformance.json / .md / .html every scan that generates an SBOM, also with --no-report (which skips only the risk report); --analyze produces it too, since that is what it measures conformance check report, with a regulatory crosswalk roll-up for every SBOM (EU CRA via BSI TR-03183-2, the US SBOM minimum elements of 2026 — reference only, no compliance determination). For an AI SBOM it also carries the G7 checks and, for each advisory element still missing, the CycloneDX fragment that would satisfy it. Names any best-effort post-process step that failed while the report was generated, so a pass is not read as proof every step ran cleanly; does not affect the pass/fail result or any individual check. See a rendered example {Project}_{Version}_ai-profile.json / .md AI SBOM (--model, or --analyze on an SBOM with a model component) AI compliance profile: G7 rollup, the closable gaps with their reference links, license-flagged components, regulatory crosswalk, and the model risk assessment (riskAssessment: per-model ok/conditional/caution/review verdicts with conditions, reasons and the usage scenario; guidance, not legal advice). The same rollup opens the conformance HTML, so there is no separate HTML profile {Project}_{Version}_scancode.json --deep-license raw scancode result {Project}_{Version}_files.json a source-having scan (a firmware scan always; other modes when --deep-license did not already produce _scancode.json) ScanCode-shaped file-tree inventory (structure only, no licenses) backing the source-tree view {Project}_{Version}_source.json a source-having scan snapshot of the scanned tree's file content, backing the file viewer (the scanned tree itself does not outlive the container) {Project}_{Version}_input.json --analyze the supplier SBOM's own format, spec version, tool and authorship, captured before the CycloneDX conversion rewrites all of it {Project}_{Version}_yocto_vex.json a Yocto build (a build directory named directly, or --analyze on one) how many CVEs the build already patched or judged not applicable — numbers not recoverable from the CycloneDX output or the security report, which list only what is still unresolved {Project}_{Version}_vex.json web UI only, saved when a judgement (affected / not affected / fixed / under investigation, with an optional note) is recorded against a CVE on the Vulnerabilities screen the judgements recorded for this scan, keyed by component and CVE. Not produced by the CLI, and absent until the first judgement is saved for a given scan. Unlike every other file here, it is not regenerated by a scan and is not removed by re-scanning the same project and version: a judgement recorded against an earlier scan survives scanning it again {Project}_{Version}_vex.cdx.json web UI only, built when you press Export VEX on the Vulnerabilities screen (needs at least one recorded judgement) the judgements from _vex.json as a standalone CycloneDX VEX document that another tool can read, at 1.7 when the scan's SBOM is 1.7 and at 1.6 otherwise. The four states map to CycloneDX analysis.state values (affected to exploitable, not affected to not_affected, fixed to resolved, under investigation to in_triage), and the note goes into analysis.detail. No justification is written, because the screen collects free text and CycloneDX allows only a fixed list. Each entry points at a copy of its component (name, version, PURL) held in the document itself, so the file stands alone. A judgement whose component is not in the SBOM is left out, and the screen says how many; firmware findings are the usual case, since their name and version come from the binary. It is rebuilt on every export and removed when the same project and version is scanned again, so export again afterwards {Project}_{Version}_vex_imported.json --vex <file> on the CLI, or Import VEX on the Vulnerabilities screen in the web UI, with a CycloneDX VEX document the statements from a supplier's VEX document that apply to a component of this scan's SBOM, with the product the document describes. Kept apart from your own judgements in _vex.json: a received statement never overwrites one, and the screen labels the two separately. The four states are mapped from CycloneDX analysis.state (exploitable to affected, not_affected and false_positive to not affected, resolved and resolved_with_pedigree to fixed, in_triage to under investigation); any other state is ignored. A document whose product or version differs from the scanned SBOM's root is refused and nothing is saved. A successful import replaces this file; a refused or empty one leaves the previous file as it was. A statement that names the product itself is stored once, without a component, and applies to every finding of that CVE that has none of its own. Like _vex.json, it is not removed by re-scanning the same project and version {Project}_{Version}_reachability.cdx.json --reachability on a Go source or Go executable scan, when govulncheck could read the Go vulnerability database govulncheck's judgement of each Go advisory against a component of the SBOM (same module and version), as a standalone CycloneDX 1.6 VEX document. analysis.state is not_affected when the affected code is not reached, with justification code_not_present when the module is required but no affected package is in the build, or code_not_reachable when the package is there but no affected function is called (or linked in an executable). It is exploitable when the code is reached. analysis.detail says which, with the call path or the symbol. id is the advisory's CVE when it has one, with its Go and other ids in references. In a source scan, metadata.properties record what was covered: bomlens:reachability:goos, goarch, build-tags and modules. The security report reads it: each finding it covers carries bomlens:reachability (state, justification, detail, level, mode) in _security.json, and the document has a Reachability summary {Project}_{Version}_vendored.cdx.json --identify-vendored on a source scan, with the opt-in SCANOSS image vendored open-source components identified inside the source tree (SCANOSS) {Project}_{Version}_security_trivy.json with the security report, when another engine (grype, cve-bin-tool, Yocto) added results to it Trivy's own result, kept apart before the merge into _security.json bomlens-events.jsonl BOMLENS_EVENTS=file progress events, one JSON object per line. See Engine contract bomlens-result.json always the run's result manifest: how it ended, each step's outcome, and the role of each output file. See Engine contract {Project}_{Version}_security_epss.json whenever the security report is generated EPSS score and KEV status per vulnerability (null/false when generated offline), used to prioritize the security report {Project}_{Version}_bom.json.sig --sign cosign signature (with --spdx, a _bom.spdx.json.sig is produced too, and an AI scan adds _bom.spdx3.json.sig; a draft is signed too, since the signature says where the file came from, not that it is complete) {new}_model-diff.json --diff <old.json> <new.json> AI-model drift report comparing two already-generated SBOMs: matched model verdict/license/hash changes, plus any component present in only one of the two files. Named after the newer input (<new>_bom.json → <new>_model-diff.json), not {Project}_{Version} — --diff takes no project or version of its own

{P} = project name, {V} = version (special characters are normalized to _).

The conditions above are the CLI flags. In the web UI and the desktop app the same choices are the generation options on the New scan screen — Notice and Security report — and every file produced is listed in the Artifacts section of the results, downloadable per format or as one ZIP. SPDX is not a scan option there: the SBOM card in that section has an Export as SPDX 2.3 button that converts the finished BOM whenever you need it, and the converted file joins the artifact list and the ZIP. The UI has no signing, so an SPDX exported that way is unsigned; use --spdx --sign in the CLI when you need a signature. See Web UI and desktop app.

docs.title: The declared AI service
docs.text:
An AI declaration (--ai-declare, or the declaration saved in the web UI) can describe the service the model runs in with a top-level service object, and give the model a few values a scan cannot read. A service is accepted only when the document describes a model, not a dataset, and one that holds no value at all counts as not declared. The AI model guide explains what these are for.

Key Value name the service's name. Required packageVersion its version. Required downloadLocation the address where the service is offered (a URI). Required suppliedBy the organization that provides it, {"type": "Organization", "name": "..."}. Required releaseTime when it was released, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ. Required informationAboutApplication what the service is for, in words domain[] the fields it serves, in words autonomyType whether a person is involved in its decisions: yes (fully automatic, no person involved), no (a person is involved) or noAssertion (not known) inputModality[], outputModality[] the kinds of input and output: text, image, audio, video, timeseries, structured, code, other dataFlows[] the data going in and out, each {flow, classification, name, description, source[], destination[]}. flow is inbound, outbound, bi-directional or unknown. classification is required (up to 200 characters) and says what the data is, such as personal data. name and description are optional words; the description says what the service does with the data. source[] and destination[] are addresses (URIs) standardCompliance[] the standards the service follows, by name disclosureUrl a public page about the service's use of AI (a URI) externalModels[] AI models the service calls through an API, each {key, name, suppliedBy, packageVersion, endpoint}. key (lowercase letters, digits, ., _ and -, up to 64, unique in the list) and name are required, and endpoint is a URI

The required keys are the ones SPDX requires of the service; the document stays a draft until they are given. The declaration's model takes five more keys:

Key Value inputModality[], outputModality[] the model's input and output kinds, with the same values as the service's trainingComputeFlops the compute used to train the model in floating-point operations, a positive decimal number written as a string, such as "3.2e24" or "1500000" trainingComputeBasis how that figure was counted, in words adversarialTesting whether adversarial testing was done: yes, no or noAssertion

In the SPDX 3.0.1 document the service is an ai_AIPackage with software_primaryPurpose application, linked to the model by a dependsOn relationship with the scope runtime, and each external model is a software_Package with the purpose model. The data flows, the input and output kinds and the model's regulatory values are CycloneDX property extensions: bomlens:service:dataFlow (one per flow, holding it as compact serviceData JSON), bomlens:service:input and :output, bomlens:model:input and :output, and bomlens:regulatory:*.

A scan also writes them into the CycloneDX SBOM, in a step that runs after the declared dataset sources are read and before the risk assessment and the G7 checks:

Location Content services[], bom-ref service:declared/<name> the service: name, version, provider.name, endpoints[0] (its address), description (what it is for), data[] (the data flows as serviceData), an externalReferences entry of type documentation (the disclosure page), and the properties bomlens:service:domain, :autonomyType, :input, :output and :releaseTime services[], bom-ref service:declared-external/<key> each external model: name, version, provider.name, endpoints and bomlens:service:declarationKey dependencies[] the service depends on the model's bom-ref and on each external model declarations.claims[] one claim per standard, with the service as target, the standard's name as predicate, and the reasoning "publisher's declaration, not verified by BomLens" the model component the properties bomlens:regulatory:trainingComputeFlops, :trainingComputeBasis and :adversarialTesting, and the input and output kinds as modelCard.modelParameters.inputs[] and outputs[] ({"format": "text"})

Every service written this way carries bomlens:origin=declared-input and bomlens:service:kind (application or external-model), and the application service carries bomlens:service:declarationDigest. On the model component, a bomlens:declared property names each location filled from the declaration (a property name, or a modelCard path; modelCard and modelCard.modelParameters themselves when the step created them). Where the scan had already recorded inputs or outputs, those are kept and a bomlens:declared:observedKept property names them. bomlens:model:declarationDigest records which declaration the model values came from. A modelCard.modelParameters created only to hold declared formats does not count as a model card in the G7 checks. The step can run again on the same SBOM: what an earlier run wrote is removed first, so a declaration without a service removes the old one, and a declaration the SPDX converter refuses is not applied at all.

The G7 system-level elements read the declared service, and an element met by it reports "present (publisher's declaration, not verified by BomLens)". The SPDX 2.3 export and --diff do not carry services. BomLens v1.13 and earlier refuse a declaration that has a service or one of the new model keys, with "unknown key(s)".

docs.title: SBOM structure
docs.text:
bomFormat          "CycloneDX"
specVersion        "1.6" ("1.7" with --spec-version 1.7)
metadata
  ├── timestamp    generation time (ISO 8601)
  └── component    project info (name, version, type)
components[]
  ├── type         "library" | "framework" | "application"
  ├── name         component name
  ├── version      version
  ├── purl         Package URL (unique identifier)
  ├── supplier     who supplied the component (when the package metadata names one)
  └── licenses[]   license info (SPDX ID)
compositions[]     dependency-graph completeness (see below)

For the per-language PURL format, see Supported ecosystems.

A component's supplier.name comes from what its package metadata already says, and from nothing else: the publisher the generator read (a Maven POM's <organization>, an npm publisher), the authors it read (PyPI, RubyGems, Composer), or the older author field, in that order. Anything in angle brackets is dropped, and so is a pair of parentheses or square brackets that holds only an email address or a URL, which removes the email address and URL of an npm-style Name <email> (url). Other parentheses stay, so Example (Holdings), Inc. is kept as it is. An email address or a URL (http://, https://, ftp://, www.) elsewhere in the value is dropped too, along with an unclosed parenthesis in front of it, so Alice <a@x.org>, Bob <b@y.org> gives Alice, Bob, Jane Doe jane@example.org gives Jane Doe and Bob <b@x.org>; Carol <c@y.org> gives Bob; Carol. A value that is only an email address or only a URL is not used, and several authors are joined with commas. The property bomlens:supplierSource names the field used (publisher, authors or author). A component with none of these has no supplier, and one that already has a supplier keeps it. Nested components follow the same rule. Distribution and firmware packages (pkg:deb, pkg:rpm, pkg:apk, pkg:alpm, pkg:opkg, pkg:generic) and operating-system components are not given a supplier: the publisher a generator reads for them is the package's maintainer, usually one person, and the distribution's name is not filled in by guess. A supplier's own SBOM under --analyze is left as it was written, and so is the output of --merge.

A source scan also records on metadata.component.properties whether the project pinned its versions: bomlens:source:versionPinning is pinned when a lock file exists, or every line of requirements.txt has an exact version, and unpinned when a requirements.txt, package.json, pyproject.toml, setup.py or setup.cfg has no lock file next to it and does not fix every version. For unpinned, the versions in the SBOM are what a fresh install resolved on the day of the scan, not necessarily the ones you ran. The web UI shows a notice, and the risk report states it under the vulnerability counts. The property is absent when the scan could not tell.

docs.title: Dependency-graph completeness
docs.text:
A generated SBOM carries a compositions[0].aggregate entry stating how complete its dependency graph is:

Value Meaning complete The scan found positive evidence the graph was fully resolved: an ecosystem's lock/resolve step succeeded, or a lockfile was already committed, plus at least one dependency edge. incomplete A known failure affected the scan: the syft fallback ran instead of cdxgen, a firmware package-cataloging step failed, or a Poetry project with no poetry.lock was converted only in part or its dependencies could not be resolved. unknown Nothing in the SBOM confirms the graph is complete. This is the default whenever there is no positive evidence either way, for example an image/rootfs/firmware/binary scan (syft alone cannot see inter-package dependencies), an AI-model, dataset or merged SBOM, or a Maven source scan (no reliable signal tells a resolved graph apart from a degraded one). unknown is not a defect; it means the tool found no basis to judge, not that something went wrong.

An analyzed supplier SBOM's own compositions declaration, if it has one, is never overwritten.

The conformance check report's transitive-dependency check notes the declared value in its detail text (e.g. "12 edge(s), declared complete"), without changing the check's pass/fail status.

A preprocessing label that ran, or was satisfied by an already-committed lockfile, is recorded in the bomlens:prep-step-applied property regardless of success or failure; bomlens:pipeline-step-failed records only the failures. aggregate above is decided from both together.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: Full options, analysis modes, CI/CD integration, and troubleshooting for BomLens.

docs.title: Options reference
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh [options]

Windows: the commands here are for macOS/Linux. Pick one of the following. See Getting started for installation.

  • Replace ./scripts/scan-sbom.sh with scripts\scan-sbom.bat (needs Git Bash).
  • Under WSL2, run the commands as-is.
  • To work without a command line, double-click scripts\sbom-ui.bat, or download the desktop app.
Option Default Description --project <name> — (required) Project name --version <version> — (required) Project version --supplier <supplier> — The supplier of the product this SBOM describes, written as "Name <https://...>" (recorded as its url) or "Name <email>" (recorded as a contact email), in metadata.component.supplier; "<https://...>" without a name records only the URL. A value that is empty after trimming writes nothing. metadata.supplier is left alone, since it would read as the SBOM's author. A bare name is recorded with a warning, since the bsi-tr-03183-2 profile needs a URL or email for it. Not written under --analyze, which keeps the supplier's own SBOM as it is; a Yocto build directory given as --target is scanned through the same path but its SBOM is this scan's, so it is written there --target <target> current directory What to analyze: a directory (source tree, or an OS rootfs / staging build output), a Docker image, a binary file, or a .zip/.tar.gz archive. A Yocto build directory is recognized as such, and the image SBOM it published under tmp/deploy/images/ is analyzed instead of the build tree being walked (see the supplier SBOM guide). A folder that is not a source tree (no manifest, lockfile or build file at its top level) and directly holds one root filesystem or one firmware image (by signature or a firmware extension such as .bix or .trx; .bin and .img by signature only), such as a release images/ folder, is scanned as that root filesystem or image, and the scan says so. A folder with executables, shared libraries, node_modules or model files at its top level, or more than 20 top-level files, stays a source scan. When it holds several, the scan stops and lists the --target to use for each --git <url> — Shallow-clone a git/GitHub URL and analyze it as source (private repos: GIT_TOKEN env var) --branch <ref> default branch Branch, tag, or commit of the --git target (alias --ref) --exclude <path> — Leave a path out of a source scan. Repeatable. The path is relative to the scanned folder (for example --exclude vendor/legacy); globs, absolute paths and .. are rejected. The scan runs on a copy of the tree without the excluded paths, so the build, the license scan and the file tree all skip them. A path that does not exist is reported and ignored --firmware false Force firmware mode on the --target file, or on a --target folder holding an unpacked image such as a root filesystem from the build (opt-in firmware image). A root filesystem folder with no package database switches to it on its own when the firmware image is present --as-source false Scan a directory --target as a source tree, as it is: no switch to a root filesystem or firmware image the folder holds, and no Yocto build directory or root filesystem recognition. Cannot be combined with --firmware --analyze <sbom> — Validate and analyze a supplier SBOM (alias --sbom). CycloneDX/SPDX. Mutually exclusive with --target --model <ref> — Generate an AI SBOM (CycloneDX 1.7 ML-BOM). A HuggingFace model id (owner/name) goes through the OWASP AIBOM Generator (opt-in bomlens-aibom image; fetches model-card metadata over the network). A Figshare item — its page URL, its DOI, or the item number — is described as a dataset from the public item endpoint, with no account and no opt-in image; an institutional DOI that does not carry "figshare" cannot be told apart from any other DOI, so give the item URL for those. A HuggingFace dataset, given as datasets/<owner>/<name>, as https://huggingface.co/datasets/<owner>/<name> (anything after the name, such as /tree/main, is ignored) or as hf:<owner>/<name>, is described as a dataset in the base image, and the datasets its card lists under source_datasets are read too (AIBOM_DATASET_DEPTH, AIBOM_DATASET_MAX_LOOKUPS). A bare owner/name is always a model id, because the hub uses the same form for both. A gated or private dataset needs HF_TOKEN. Mutually exclusive with --target/--analyze/--git/--merge --model-file <path> — Read one AI model file and describe it from its own header: GGUF, safetensors, PyTorch (.pt/.pth/.ckpt), pickle, npz, npy or ONNX. Offline, no HuggingFace account, and it works on a model that was never published. What can be filled depends on the format — GGUF carries a name, a license and an architecture, while safetensors usually carries only tensor shapes, and a field the file does not declare is left empty rather than guessed. A .gguf/.safetensors/.pt/… path passed to --target is read this way too. Mutually exclusive with --target/--analyze/--git --license <spdx-id> — The outbound license the project is distributed under (e.g. Apache-2.0). Recorded on the SBOM's root component, with acknowledgement concluded (the distribution licence), and used to flag dependencies whose terms clash with it. It replaces a root license the generator read. A source scan cannot infer this — cdxgen leaves the root license empty for maven and gradle — so without it no conflict verdict is produced; a license read from the project manifest instead only fills an empty root license, as declared. A supplier SBOM's own root license under --analyze is never replaced; for a Yocto build directory given as --target it is recorded on the image. An SPDX License List id (in any letter case) is written as license.id, a LicenseRef- or DocumentRef-...:LicenseRef- name (prefixes in any letter case) as license.name, and an expression as expression: SPDX ids and LicenseRef- names joined by AND or OR, WITH followed by an SPDX exception id, and balanced parentheses, with operators in any letter case and ids written in the SPDX list's spelling. Anything else, free text such as Proprietary or an expression such as Proprietary or commercial or MIT AND, is refused with the reason and, for free text, the LicenseRef- name to use. In the scans that record it (a source scan, a root filesystem, a Yocto build directory) it is refused when the scan starts, before anything is generated, whoever started it (CLI, web UI or a CI job); the CLI refuses it before starting a container. A licence read from the project manifest that does not fit is left out with a warning --sbom-author <name> — The entity that generated the SBOM — the organisation or person running the scan, not the tool and not whoever wrote the software. Recorded in metadata.authors, using the full name without acronyms. Nothing in a scan can discover it, so the field is left out of the SBOM when it is not given rather than filled with a placeholder. Written as Name <email> (for example "Example Corp <sbom@example.com>"), the email is recorded too, as the bsi-tr-03183-2 profile asks of the SBOM creator. Not written under --analyze, except for a Yocto build directory given as --target, whose SBOM this scan generates --ai-declare <file> — For an AI model or dataset scan: the publisher's declaration (JSON) of what a scan cannot read, such as release dates, who made the model and the data, which datasets trained or tested it, the base model revision and the distributed weights scope. Most declared values are written only to the SPDX 3.0.1 AI document. The exceptions are the service the model runs in (service) and the model's input and output kinds, training compute and adversarial testing, which also go into the CycloneDX SBOM, marked as the publisher's declaration (see the example below). Every AI scan writes an empty one to start from, {Project}_{Version}_ai-declaration.template.json. A file that names a field, value, dataset or base model the scan does not have is refused with the reasons, and the document is written without it, as a draft. The accepted file is kept as {Project}_{Version}_ai-declaration.json and applied again on the next scan of the same version. Given alone, without --model, --model-file or --target, it describes a model that has no hub repository or file yet (MODE=AIDECLARE, base image): the base models in model.baseModels[].ref and the datasets in datasets[].ref (huggingface:<owner>/<name>) are read from the hub by id, datasets[].local lists data the hub does not hold, and the model is named by --project and --version. Without a declared download address and supplier, the SPDX document stays a draft. Not offered with --ui (use the Models & datasets screen) or --diff --no-spdx3 false For an AI model or dataset scan: do not write the SPDX 3.0.1 AI document, its check or the declaration template --vex <file> — A CycloneDX VEX document (JSON) a supplier sent for this product. The statements that apply to a component of the scanned SBOM are kept in {Project}_{Version}_vex_imported.json; the SBOM and the security report are not changed. Turns the security report on too (as --deep-cve does), because the statements are shown on its findings: open the scan folder in the web UI to see them on the vulnerability rows. A document for a different product or version, or one that is not CycloneDX VEX, is reported and skipped, and the scan still completes; a document with no applicable statement leaves an earlier _vex_imported.json as it was. Not offered with --ui (use Import VEX on the Vulnerabilities screen) or --diff --component-versions <file> — For a firmware, root filesystem or binary scan: a CSV file, name,version,reason, giving the version of components the scan found but could not read a version for. The third column is optional (a two-column name,version file is read as before); with the version left empty it says why there is none: own-code, not-open-source or version-unknown, recorded on the component as bomlens:versionReason. A reason on a row that also has a version, on a component the scan read a version for, or on a name the scan did not find is ignored with a warning. A version the scan read from the delivered files is kept and a warning shows both; a name the scan did not find is added as a component marked bomlens:identifiedBy = supplier-declared. Every such scan writes the components still missing a version to {Project}_{Version}_component-versions.template.csv in this format. A file over 256 KiB, with a malformed row or with any other reason value is refused: the scan still writes its files, without those versions, and exits 1 with the reason. A row with neither a version nor a reason is skipped. See the firmware guide --components <file> sbom-declared.cdx.json at the scan target root, when it exists For a source scan or a Yocto build: a CycloneDX file (JSON) listing the components the scan cannot find, such as your own build outputs and third-party parts added by hand. Repeat the option for several files; with it, sbom-declared.cdx.json is not read. Each component needs the property bomlens:origin (first-party or third-party), and a third-party one needs a version; a first-party one without a version takes --version. A build output named in bomlens:artifact (a path relative to the scan target root) gets its SHA-512 and SHA-256 hashes and the bsi:component:filename, bsi:component:executable, bsi:component:archive and bsi:component:structured properties (structured or unstructured as BSI TR-03183-2 defines it), read from the file; a value the declaration gives for executable, archive or structured is kept instead. Each build output is also named on an externalReferences entry of type distribution carrying its SHA-512, as BSI TR-03183-2 section 8 does: its url is the component's bomlens:distribution-url property when given (an http or https URL, or a relative path without .., in which a % must start a %XX escape), otherwise the build output's path; a component with several build outputs gets one per file and cannot give bomlens:distribution-url. A licence given without an acknowledgement is written as concluded, the distribution licence; an acknowledgement the declaration gives is kept. A component may use only these CycloneDX fields: name, version, bom-ref, group, description, copyright, cpe, purl, publisher, author, mime-type, type, scope, tags, supplier, manufacturer, authors, hashes, licenses, externalReferences and properties; any other field, nested components included, is refused by name. A license id must be an id on the SPDX License List, so an unknown id is refused; give a license that is not on the list as name. A file that breaks these rules is refused, for example one over 4 MiB, a component without a valid bomlens:origin, a named file that is missing or outside the scan target, or the same name and version declared twice: the scan stops before the SBOM is finished, keeps the SBOM written so far as {Project}_{Version}_bom.refused.json (not _bom.json) and exits 1, naming the file and component. For a Yocto build directory given as --target, a component names its recipe (PN) in bomlens:yocto-recipe instead of a build output, and no default file is read: the declaration goes on every package installed in the image whose recipe the build recorded as that PN (a package whose recipe the build did not record is not matched by its name; a multilib or SDK variant such as lib32-<PN> or nativesdk-<PN> is a recipe of its own, declared separately, and a warning names any the image installs), which keep their name, version, purl and CPE and get the declared type, supplier, licence (concluded) and bomlens:origin. The files and hashes the SPDX document records for each package (SHA-256, and SHA-512 from Yocto 6.1) are nested under it as file components with their bsi:component:filename; no package hash is made up. A recipe that installed no package, a version other than the build's, bomlens:artifact beside bomlens:yocto-recipe, hashes, purl, cpe, bom-ref, group or mime-type on a recipe declaration, or a component added by name that has the name of an installed package (declare that one by its recipe), is refused the same way. In any scan a declaration may not carry the properties the scan itself writes (bomlens:identifiedBy, bomlens:yocto:recipe, bomlens:layer, bomlens:yocto:arch). Refused with --analyze: an SBOM passed there is received, and is not changed. Not offered with --ui or --diff; the web UI reads sbom-declared.cdx.json at the root of the folder it scans, a source tree or a Yocto build directory. See the declared components guide --no-components false For a source scan: do not read sbom-declared.cdx.json at the scan target root, for example in a scan made before the build outputs it names exist. When that file is refused because a build output is missing, the message points to this option. Cannot be combined with --components; not offered with --ui (the web UI's Read sbom-declared.cdx.json switch does the same) or --diff --usage <scenario> — Tailor the AI model risk assessment (--model and --model-file) to how the model will be used: internal, product, redistribute or outputs-only. Only the license conditions that bind that scenario decide the verdict, and the report states which scenario it was judged for. Unset judges against every condition --merge <a.json> <b.json> … — Merge two or more CycloneDX SBOMs into one, dedupe by purl, and stamp the root component with --project/--version. Optional — for a server SBOM when an external system needs a single product BOM; otherwise keep the layers separate (see the server SBOM guide). Mutually exclusive with --target/--analyze/--git --merge-root <file> — With --merge: keep this input's specVersion and root component (for example an ML-BOM's CycloneDX 1.7 root with its model card) instead of writing a fresh root at the --spec-version version. Must be one of the --merge files; the preserved root is renamed to --project/--version --diff <old.json> <new.json> — Compare two already-generated AI-model SBOMs (--model or --model-file output) for drift: a bomlens:assessment:* verdict that got worse, a changed declared license, or a SHA-256 weight-file hash that no longer matches under the same model name/purl/HuggingFace id — the last one means the artifact behind a stable name silently changed. Needs neither --project/--version nor a scan target: it only reads the two files and writes <new>_model-diff.json next to the newer one (or under --output-dir) --generate-only false Save locally only, without uploading --upload-target <target> dependency-track Upload destination: dependency-track (DT-compatible) or trusca (native ingest) --trusca <project_id> — Upload to TRUSCA (= --upload-target trusca + project id). Needs API_URL and a Bearer API_KEY --notice forced on by the risk-report default Generate the open-source notice (NOTICE, txt+html). The flag itself defaults to off; it is the risk report (on by default) that turns it on, so --no-report, not simply omitting --notice, is what skips it --security forced on by the risk-report default Generate the Trivy security report (json+md+html), including CVSS, EPSS, and CISA KEV priority signals. Same mechanism as --notice: --no-report skips it, omitting the flag alone does not --spdx false Also export the SBOM as SPDX 2.3 JSON (_bom.spdx.json), converted from the final CycloneDX output --spec-version <1.6\|1.7> 1.6 CycloneDX version of the SBOM. 1.7 has cdxgen and syft write 1.7, and an SBOM put together at 1.4, 1.5 or 1.6 is labelled 1.7, $schema included, before it is delivered. Those versions only gained fields up to 1.7, except that from 1.6 on a property must have a name, so a 1.4 or 1.5 property without one is removed as the SBOM is raised. An SBOM at 1.3 or older keeps its version, and so does a 1.4 SBOM at the default 1.6, which then gets no metadata.lifecycles (a 1.5 field). NOTICE, the security report, the conformance check and the web UI read either version. AI model and dataset SBOMs are 1.7 whatever this says. Dependency-Track reads 1.7 from 4.14.4 and 5.1.0 on; an older server, or one whose version is not known, that refuses it gets a 1.6 copy (see Upload). Any other value stops the scan --all — --notice --security --spdx --no-report false Skip the open-source risk report (see below) --lang <en\|ko> en Language for the human-facing conformance and AI-profile reports (.md/.html). The SBOM and the JSON reports stay English regardless --conformance-profile <default\|skt-submission\|bsi-tr-03183-2> default Conformance check strictness. skt-submission requires 100% PURL coverage and fails on any pkg:generic identifier, matching the SKT supplier submission review. It also adds a required "Version needed" row, which fails only on components with neither a version nor a reason (fill them with --component-versions) and lists the ones with a reason as explained by the supplier, and an advisory "No upstream purl" row for versioned components without an upstream purl, which SK Telecom checks separately. For a firmware, root filesystem, binary or Yocto build directory scan, and under --analyze for an SBOM marked bomlens:scanMode by one, the name+version, PURL coverage, pkg:generic and transitive-dependency rows warn instead of failing on what those two rows already cover, since such a scan records packages found rather than a dependency graph. The profile accepts pkg:sourceforge and pkg:gnu, and says in the summary that {Project}_{Version}_bom.json is the one file to submit. The web UI's submission-review screen defaults to skt-submission; the CLI does not, so pair it with --analyze explicitly. In every profile, a component the --components file added in this scan with bomlens:origin first-party, a supplier and a SHA-512 needs no purl: it is left out of PURL coverage, the pkg:generic row and the upstream-purl row, and listed on an advisory row by name. A third-party one is not, and nothing is exempted under --analyze. bsi-tr-03183-2 measures the SBOM against BSI TR-03183-2 v2.1.0: CycloneDX 1.6 or later (SPDX 3.0 or later), a timestamp, an SBOM creator with an email or URL (metadata.manufacturer, or metadata.authors with an email, which --sbom-author "Name <email>" writes), and a dependency graph that reaches every component from the product are required; the graph row warns when the SBOM does not state its completeness (compositions), and a component without its own dependencies entry is listed on an advisory row. The product (metadata.component) needs a creator with a URL or email, a name, a version and a concluded licence (--license writes the licence and --supplier the creator), and its filename, SHA-512 and file properties when it names a file. For each component the --components file added, the creator (supplier or manufacturer with a URL or email), name and version, and the distribution licence as an SPDX identifier, expression or LicenseRef- name with acknowledgement concluded are required; for one that names a build output, so are its file name, SHA-512 (on the component, its files or a distribution reference) and executable, archive and structured properties. A declared library or framework with no file of its own is listed on an advisory row; a declared component of any other type without one fails the file rows. The components the scan found are measured on one advisory row, with counts and each component's gaps, and do not move the result; in the SBOM a scan generated from a Yocto build directory, a SHA-512 missing from a package the build recorded is reported there as not in the source SBOM. For such a package declared by recipe (bomlens:yocto-recipe), a SHA-512, file name or file properties the build did not record are reported the same way on the declared rows, as a warning rather than a failure. A received SBOM (--analyze) gets no such allowance, whatever properties its components carry. PURL coverage is advisory in this profile --license-registry off Ask the package registry (deps.dev) for the licence of a component that has none, and check a component's single strong-copyleft or non-commercial licence (GPL, AGPL, SSPL, BUSL, CC-BY-NC) against it. When the registry says otherwise its answer replaces the recorded one, and the old value is kept in bomlens:license:superseded; licences written this way carry bomlens:licenseSource = registry (deps.dev). A licence with its text, a url or a concluded acknowledgement is never checked, and with --analyze only missing licences are filled. Uses the network --resolve-purl off --analyze only: ask each package repository whether the identifiers in the submitted SBOM name packages that exist, and add the answer to the conformance check report as an advisory row. The only part of the check that uses the network. An identifier that resolves to nothing is reported, never failed, because a package published only to an internal repository answers the same way; PURL_RESOLVE_IGNORE skips namespaces you know are internal --deep-license false Precise license detection with scancode in the project's own files (opt-in bomlens-deep-license image, pulled automatically; when it cannot be pulled, the scan runs on the base image without the licence scan). With --deep-cve as well, the licence scan runs first in this image and post-processing then runs on the deep-cve image, so both _scancode.json and _security_grype.json are written --deep-cve false Add a second CVE-matching pass via grype's NVD CPE matcher (opt-in bomlens-deep-cve image, pulled automatically; a source scan runs its post-processing step on it, and when it cannot be pulled, the source scan goes on without the grype match; with a SBOM_SCANNER_IMAGE that is a local build, a version before 1.13.2 or another name and no SBOM_DEEP_CVE_IMAGE, post-processing stays on that image, which runs the match only if it has grype, also with --deep-license). Recovers NVD-only CVEs that Trivy misses, mostly for older Maven libraries, since BomLens attaches an NVD-matchable CPE to Maven components specifically; implies --security. Findings not verified against the live NVD version range are flagged version-unverified in the report. See the deep CVE matching guide --reachability false Go source, or a Go executable given with --target: judge with govulncheck whether the code each Go advisory names is reached, from the source's call graph or from the executable's symbols. An advisory whose code is not reached is recorded as not_affected (with code_not_present when the affected package is not in the build, code_not_reachable when it is but no affected function is reached) in {Project}_{Version}_reachability.cdx.json (CycloneDX VEX), marked on its finding in _security.json, listed in its own "Not reachable" section of the security report, and left out of that report's totals, the risk report's and --fail-on vulnerability=. One whose code is reached is exploitable, with the call path. Implies --security. govulncheck reads the Go vulnerability database (vuln.go.dev) over the network; when it cannot, the step is skipped and the report is as without the option. A source scan runs govulncheck in the Go image of stage 1, for each Go module in the tree (up to 20) and for GOOS linux, darwin and windows (GOARCH amd64) with the default build tags; code built only under a custom build tag is not covered. With --ui it is chosen per scan in the web UI's advanced scan options instead. See Go reachability --identify-vendored false Identify open source copied (vendored) into C/C++ source that has no package manager. Matches file fingerprints against the OSSKB service (included in the published image; sends hashes, not source). See the identify bundled OSS guide --verify-weights false With --model: download the repo's pickle-format weight files (.bin/.pt/.pth/.ckpt — the ones that execute code on load) and run the same local picklescan verification --model-file runs, instead of only trusting HuggingFace's own scan (bomlens:hf:scan:*). safetensors/GGUF/ONNX weights are never downloaded — they cannot execute code on load, so there is nothing for picklescan to check. Real network and disk cost (bounded by AIBOM_VERIFY_MAX_FILES/AIBOM_VERIFY_MAX_BYTES, default 5 files / 2 GiB each), unlike the metadata-only ENRICH_HF_SECURITY lookup, which is why this is opt-in. AI-model scans only --byte-stable false Deterministic (reproducible) SBOM output --detection <how> auto How a source scan finds its dependencies: build resolves them in a cdxgen language image, static reads the lock file and does not build (no language image to pull, about 5 to 10 seconds shorter; a project with no complete lock file comes out short, a workspace takes its members' dependencies in, and the copyright notices a build reads from downloaded packages, for example 73 of 98 crates in a Rust project, are not filled), auto reads statically only when a package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lock or gradle.lockfile covers the whole tree and builds otherwise. A static scan fills the licenses a lock file does not carry from the package registry (the same lookup as --license-registry), so auto builds under --byte-stable or FETCH_LICENSE=false. DETECTION=<how> in the environment does the same. The SBOM records which way it was made (bomlens:detection) --fail-on-conformance false Exit 2 if this scan's own conformance check report says "fail" (exit 3 if no conformance check report was produced for this scan). Not offered with --ui. See Exit codes --fail-on <condition> — Exit 4 when this scan meets the condition, or 5 when it cannot be judged from what the scan produced. Repeat the option for several conditions. The conditions are a closed list: vulnerability=<critical\|high\|medium\|low> (a finding at that severity or worse; turns the security report on), malicious-package (a component flagged as a known malicious package), license-conflict (a component incompatible with the license the product is distributed under; the SBOM's root component has to record it, which --license does for source and rootfs scans and a supplier SBOM carries itself, otherwise it cannot be judged), empty-result (the scan identified no software: no component is left once operating-system and file entries are set aside, so a rootfs or image scan that names no package counts as empty), license-coverage=<0-100> (fewer than that percent of those same components declare a license; a license of NOASSERTION or NONE is not a declaration, and the percentage is rounded down; the value is required, has no default and takes no leading zero). Both read the scan's own conformance check report, so a scan that wrote none cannot be judged, nor can one whose SBOM format the report did not measure (an SPDX 3.0 document that could not be converted). license-coverage= cannot be judged on a scan with no such component either (use empty-result for that). They leave the conformance verdict itself unchanged. Findings are counted as the security report counts them: once per package and id, with the kernel's advisories left out. --vex statements are not applied, so a finding the supplier declared not affected still counts; a finding --reachability judged not reachable does not. vulnerability= is not available for AI model and dataset inputs, which have no dependencies to scan, and neither is empty-result. Not offered with --ui or --diff. See Exit codes --sign false cosign signature (COSIGN_KEY required) --output-dir <dir> current directory Base directory for outputs (alias -o). Each scan lands in a {Project}_{Version}/ subfolder under it, keeping the bundle together and out of the source tree --timestamp false Append _YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS to the run subfolder so repeat scans of the same project and version are kept side by side instead of overwritten. Folder name only; SBOM bytes are unchanged --ui — Launch the local web UI --mount <dir> — With --ui: expose an extra host directory to the web UI as a read-only target for the Directory path input (repeatable). Lets the UI scan an OS tree outside the launch folder — including the running host OS with --mount /. Results still save under the launch folder --help — Print help

ANALYZE mode (--analyze) is an exception to six of these. --project/--version/--license/--sbom-author/--supplier never overwrite what a supplier's own SBOM already declares: its existing name, version, root license, authorship and supplier are a fact about the document, not something this run has the authority to replace. --no-report has no effect because the risk report is always generated for a supplier SBOM under review. When the submitted SBOM is missing one of these fields outright (no root license, no metadata.authors, no product supplier), the flag still cannot fill it in; the field stays empty and the conformance check judges accordingly.

Environment variables adjust the behavior.

Variable Default Description SBOM_SCANNER_IMAGE ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens:latest Override the scanner image SBOM_FIRMWARE_IMAGE Follows SBOM_SCANNER_IMAGE when it is a BomLens image name with a registry path and a tag of 1.13.2 or later, or a tag that is not a version (same registry path and tag: .../bomlens:1.13.2 gives .../bomlens-firmware:1.13.2), else ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens-firmware:latest Image used for firmware analysis SBOM_AIBOM_IMAGE Follows SBOM_SCANNER_IMAGE when it is a BomLens image name with a registry path and a tag of 1.13.2 or later, or a tag that is not a version (same registry path and tag: .../bomlens:1.13.2 gives .../bomlens-aibom:1.13.2), else ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens-aibom:latest Image used for AI model (ML-BOM) generation SBOM_DEEP_CVE_IMAGE Follows SBOM_SCANNER_IMAGE when it is a BomLens image name with a registry path and a tag of 1.13.2 or later, or a tag that is not a version (same registry path and tag: .../bomlens:1.13.2 gives .../bomlens-deep-cve:1.13.2), else ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens-deep-cve:latest Image used for --deep-cve (grype CPE matching), and by the same toggle in the web UI SBOM_DEEP_LICENSE_IMAGE Follows SBOM_SCANNER_IMAGE under the same condition; otherwise SBOM_SCANNER_IMAGE itself; when neither is set, ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens-deep-license:latest Image a source scan's post-process step runs on with --deep-license (scancode) SBOM_OUTPUT_FLAT — Set to 1 to write artifacts flat in the output base, with no per-run subfolder (the pre-isolation layout, for CI that expects the old paths) SBOM_OUTPUT_DIR ~/sbom-output Output base for the desktop app and web UI (the CLI uses --output-dir instead). Each scan still lands in a {Project}_{Version}/ subfolder under it SBOM_UI_MOUNT_DIR — For the Windows launcher sbom-ui.bat, which takes no CLI arguments: one extra folder to expose to the web UI as a read-only Directory path target (the double-click counterpart of --ui --mount). Use a path without & ^ | < > — the launcher rejects those rather than passing a mangled mount to Docker SBOM_LANG system locale en or ko, for the Windows launchers and the desktop app. Anything that is not Korean gets English SBOM_BASH auto-detected For scan-sbom.bat: explicit path to Git Bash's bash.exe (e.g. C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe), when the launcher's own detection (deriving it from git on PATH) fails to find one that is not WSL's or a WindowsApps alias CDXGEN_IMAGE_PREFIX ghcr.io/cdxgen/ Where the cdxgen images of a source scan are pulled from (the language images and the all-in-one image): everything before the image name. On a network with no route to ghcr.io, set it to a registry mirror that holds the same images, for example registry.example/mirror/cdxgen/; the names and tags stay the same. Passed on to the web UI's source scans (--ui, sbom-ui.bat, the desktop app), and taken by the Android SDK image's build as --build-arg (that build pins its base image by digest, so the mirror must be a pull-through cache or a copy of every platform) SBOM_PULL missing Scanner image download policy, honored by both scan-sbom.sh and the Windows launcher. missing (default) pulls only when the image is absent, and otherwise quietly refreshes an already-present :latest in the background (bounded and best-effort: a stalled or offline check gives up and the run proceeds with the local image either way). always blocks and re-pulls every run, failing the run if the pull fails. never never touches the network, failing the run if the image is absent. An opt-in image that --deep-cve or --deep-license needs is pulled once when absent (once per run with always), with docker's progress shown and no time limit. With always, a pull that fails uses the copy already here; a scan that cannot get it at all, offline or with never, goes on without it and says so SBOM_IMAGE_TAR — Path to an image tar from docker save. The Windows launcher loads it instead of pulling; a file named bomlens-image.tar next to the scripts is picked up automatically. Combined with SBOM_PULL=never this gives a fully offline install CVE_BIN_TOOL_MODE auto Firmware, root filesystem and binary scans: components-only turns off the match of CPEs against the NVD CPE index in the image, while firmware binaries are still identified; any other value leaves it on. Read by the scanner container (docker run -e); the CLI does not pass it on CVE_BIN_TOOL_HOME /opt/cve-bin-tool-home Where the image keeps the NVD CPE index (cpe_match.sqlite) and its data notice. The firmware image also keeps there the placeholder cve.db cve-bin-tool needs in order to start; it holds no CVE data CVE_BIN_TOOL_DISABLE_SOURCES GAD,OSV cve-bin-tool data sources to disable during a firmware scan. GAD (GitLab Advisory) and OSV are disabled by default so identification does not reach out over the network SCANOSS_API_URL OSSKB free API Endpoint for --identify-vendored. Point at a SCANOSS commercial or self-hosted endpoint for air-gapped or high-volume use SCANOSS_API_KEY — Credential for SCANOSS_API_URL, if the endpoint requires one SCANOSS_MIN_FILES 2 Minimum number of files that must match a library before it is reported, to drop one-off downstream-fork noise. Set 1 to keep every single-file match GIT_TOKEN — Token for cloning private git repositories HF_TOKEN — HuggingFace read token for --model and for the dataset metadata lookups during AI SBOM analysis. Required for a private or gated repository, which is how you review a model before publishing it. HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN is accepted as an alias ENRICH_HF_SECURITY true Read HuggingFace's own file-security scan results (ClamAV and picklescan, per file) for --model scans and record them in the ML-BOM. Metadata only, no file download. Set false to skip the lookup AIBOM_VERIFY_MAX_FILES 5 With --verify-weights: maximum number of pickle-format weight files downloaded and scanned per model. Extra files beyond the cap are left unchecked, not queued AIBOM_VERIFY_MAX_BYTES 2147483648 (2 GiB) With --verify-weights: a weight file larger than this (by the repo's declared size, or by its actual downloaded size if that differs) is skipped rather than downloaded/scanned AIBOM_DATASET_DEPTH 3 With --model: how many levels of a dataset's own sources (source_datasets on its card) to read and judge with it. 0 reads only the datasets the model card names, as before AIBOM_DATASET_MAX_LOOKUPS 40 With --model: the most datasets one scan reads, sources included. Datasets past the limit are recorded by name as not read COSIGN_KEY — Path to the signing key used by --sign CYCLONEDX_SPEC_VERSION 1.6 Same as --spec-version. Also read by the scanner image itself, for a docker run without the CLI FETCH_LICENSE true Resolve dependency licenses during source scans. Set false to skip the lookup and run faster GOTOOLCHAIN auto Go source scans: which Go toolchain resolves the modules. By default, when go.mod asks for a newer Go than the scanner image carries, that version is downloaded. Set local to use only the image's own Go; dependency resolution then fails for such a project GOPROXY https://proxy.golang.org,direct Go source scans: proxy for module and toolchain downloads, for a network that cannot reach proxy.golang.org. GOSUMDB is passed on the same way PROJECT_LICENSE — Same as --license. The outbound license the project is distributed under, as an SPDX id. Drives the bomlens:licenseConflict verdicts and the risk report's conflict section SBOM_AUTHOR — Same as --sbom-author. The entity that generated the SBOM, recorded in metadata.authors PRODUCT_SUPPLIER — Same as --supplier. The supplier of the product, recorded in metadata.component.supplier SECURITY_ENRICH true Enrich the security report with EPSS and CISA KEV signals. Set false on air-gapped networks to skip the external lookups HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY — Passed on by name to the scan containers (the lower-case forms too). A proxy at this machine's loopback address (127.0.0.1, localhost) is not passed, since in a container that address is the container itself; Docker's own proxy settings apply then TRIVY_* — Any Trivy setting, passed on by name, for example TRIVY_DB_REPOSITORY for a database mirror or TRIVY_SKIP_DB_UPDATE=true offline. TRIVY_CACHE_DIR is not passed (a host path); use SBOM_TRIVY_CACHE SBOM_TRIVY_CACHE ~/.cache/bomlens/trivy (%LOCALAPPDATA%\bomlens\cache\trivy on Windows) A host folder kept as Trivy's cache, so its vulnerability database (about 1.5 GB) is downloaded once instead of on every scan, which saves 15 to 25 seconds per scan (the web UI's scans too). Set it to an empty value to download on every scan, as before. Scans can run side by side: only the database is shared. For an offline host, put the database there and set TRIVY_SKIP_DB_UPDATE=true. On Linux the files in it belong to root EPSS_API, KEV_URL public endpoints Mirrors for the EPSS and CISA KEV lookups SECURITY_NVD_VERIFY false With --deep-cve: verify each grype nvd:cpe finding against the live NVD version range and drop out-of-range false positives (needs NVD_API_KEY and network access; adds minutes). Off by default — findings are kept and flagged version-unverified NVD_API_KEY — NVD API key for SECURITY_NVD_VERIFY. Passed to the container by name only, never inlined into the command SYFT_REGISTRY_AUTH_USERNAME, SYFT_REGISTRY_AUTH_PASSWORD, SYFT_REGISTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SYFT_REGISTRY_AUTH_AUTHORITY — An image scan of an image the local Docker daemon does not have: credentials for its private registry (an image you can docker pull needs none). SYFT_REGISTRY_INSECURE_SKIP_TLS_VERIFY, SYFT_REGISTRY_INSECURE_USE_HTTP and SYFT_PLATFORM are passed on too. Passed by name only API_URL — Upload server URL (a DT server, or the TRUSCA base) API_KEY — Upload credential. Used as X-Api-Key for DT, as a Bearer token for TRUSCA UPLOAD_TARGET dependency-track Upload destination: dependency-track or trusca TRUSCA_PROJECT_ID — TRUSCA project id (UUID). Required when trusca TRUSCA_REF main Ingest ref label TRUSCA_RELEASE --version value Ingest release label EXTERNAL_LOOKUP true With --ui: enable the web UI's CVE/package lookup, which queries OSV.dev on demand. Set false for air-gapped runs SBOM_UPLOAD_TTL_HOURS 24 With --ui: how long an uploaded file is kept if no scan is ever started with it (a picked-then-abandoned upload). Clamped to at least 1

A short local name with no registry path, such as sbom-scanner:local, and a version tag before 1.13.2 keep the earlier defaults: ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens-<name>:latest for the opt-in images, and SBOM_SCANNER_IMAGE itself for --deep-license.

When SBOM_SCANNER_IMAGE is pinned by digest only, the opt-in images use :latest in the CLI and the web UI and the app's own version in the desktop app; to pin them as well, set each SBOM_*_IMAGE.

Source-scan resolver options such as BOMLENS_MAVEN_FULL_GRAPH are listed under Docker image environment variables. Set them in the shell that runs scan-sbom.sh and they reach dependency resolution the same way.

On Windows, environment variables set in a command prompt do not survive a double-click. The launchers therefore also read UI_PORT, SBOM_LANG, SBOM_PULL, SBOM_IMAGE_TAR, SBOM_SCANNER_IMAGE, SBOM_OUTPUT_DIR and SBOM_UI_MOUNT_DIR from a plain text file: copy scripts/bomlens.settings.example.txt to bomlens.settings.txt beside the scripts (or to %USERPROFILE%\.bomlens\settings.txt). A real environment variable always wins over the file.

Output flags are detailed in the reports guide; validating a received supplier SBOM is covered in the supplier SBOM validation.

docs.title: The AI declaration file
docs.text:
