--ai-declare takes a JSON file. Start from the {Project}_{Version}_ai-declaration.template.json an AI scan writes, and fill what applies. This one describes a model that runs in a support chat service and calls an external translation model:

{
  "schema": "bomlens-ai-declaration/1",
  "document": {"createdBy": [{"type": "Organization", "name": "Acme AI Lab"}]},
  "model": {
    "releaseTime": "2025-04-15T00:00:00Z",
    "originatedBy": [{"type": "Organization", "name": "Acme AI Lab"}],
    "inputModality": ["text"],
    "outputModality": ["text"],
    "trainingComputeFlops": "3.2e21",
    "trainingComputeBasis": "6 x parameters x training tokens, from the training logs",
    "adversarialTesting": "yes"
  },
  "service": {
    "name": "Acme Support Assistant",
    "packageVersion": "2.3.0",
    "downloadLocation": "https://support.acme.example/assistant",
    "suppliedBy": {"type": "Organization", "name": "Acme Corp"},
    "releaseTime": "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z",
    "autonomyType": "no",
    "dataFlows": [
      {"flow": "outbound", "classification": "personal data",
       "description": "Questions forwarded to the external translation model.",
       "destination": ["https://api.translate.example/v1"]}
    ],
    "externalModels": [
      {"key": "translate", "name": "Example Translate",
       "suppliedBy": {"type": "Organization", "name": "Example Inc"},
       "endpoint": "https://api.translate.example/v1"}
    ]
  }
}

./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project support-adapter --version 1.0 \
  --model "acme/support-adapter" --ai-declare declaration.json --generate-only

The service and the model's input and output kinds, training compute and adversarial testing reach the CycloneDX SBOM in the same run; everything else goes only to the SPDX 3.0.1 document. Every key and allowed value is listed under The declared AI service. BomLens v1.13 and earlier refuse a file with service or these model keys ("unknown key(s)"). --no-spdx3 cannot be combined with --ai-declare given as the only input, since most declared values have nowhere else to go.

docs.title: Where outputs go
docs.text:
Each scan is isolated in its own {Project}_{Version}/ subfolder, so the files from one run stay together and the CLI never litters the source tree it scans. That subfolder is created under a base directory:

  • CLI (scan-sbom.sh): the base is the directory you ran the command in. Override it with --output-dir <dir> (alias -o).
  • Desktop app and web UI: the base is ~/sbom-output (C:\Users\<you>\sbom-output on Windows). Override it with the SBOM_OUTPUT_DIR environment variable.

For --git or archive ingestion the clone or extract happens in a temp directory that is cleaned up on exit, and only the output subfolder remains.

A re-scan of the same project and version overwrites its subfolder by default, keeping just the latest result. Add --timestamp to keep each run instead: it appends _YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS to the folder name, for example MyApp_1.0.0_20260626-143000/. The flag changes the folder name only, not the SBOM file names or bytes, so it works together with --byte-stable.

To restore the previous flat layout, where every file is written directly in the base with no per-run subfolder, set SBOM_OUTPUT_FLAT=1. This is meant for CI that expects the old paths.

--diff has no project or version of its own, so it writes its report directly into the base directory (current directory, or --output-dir) rather than a per-run subfolder.

docs.title: What the scan prints at the end
docs.text:
With --generate-only, the CLI lists the files it produced after Analysis Complete!. If a requested file was not produced, the heading reads Analysis finished with errors instead and a warning names the missing files; the exit code stays 0, so use --fail-on to stop a pipeline on a scan that could not be judged. For every scan that measured software (not an AI model or dataset scan) it then states what the result holds:

  Components:  176 identified (purl on 100%, license declared on 96% (169 of 176))

The numbers come from the scan's own conformance measurement, so they match the licenseCoverage and softwareComponentCount fields of the conformance check report, and the purl share counts the same packages as its purl check. The purl share is shown for CycloneDX results only. A warning line follows when something is off:

  • No software was identified: the result has no components. Check that the scanned folder holds a manifest or lock file for a supported ecosystem.
  • No component declares a license: no component declares one, so license checks have nothing to work with.
  • Reduced analysis: a shallow fallback ran instead of the full analysis and only direct dependencies were identified. The line names the cause: out of disk space, out of memory, a failed download, or the dependency analyzer failing or not running.
  • Steps that failed: post-processing steps that did not complete, by name. Details are in the log above.

The last two are not shown for --analyze, because they would describe the submitted document rather than this run. The summary does not change the exit code. To fail a run on these conditions, use --fail-on empty-result or --fail-on license-coverage=<0-100>. A scanner image that predates the summary prints only the file list.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Scan succeeded 1 Scan failed (bad arguments, Docker unavailable, a required input missing, and similar) 2 --fail-on-conformance: the scan succeeded, but its own conformance check report says "fail" 3 --fail-on-conformance: the scan succeeded, but produced no conformance check report to judge 4 --fail-on: the scan succeeded, but at least one condition is met 5 --fail-on: the scan succeeded, but a condition could not be judged (for example the vulnerability database could not be downloaded, license-conflict without --license, or empty-result and license-coverage= when the scan wrote no conformance check report or the report did not measure the SBOM's format), or the scan produced no result to judge

2 to 5 are used only when the matching option is given; every scan that uses neither exits 0 or 1. Every --fail-on condition is printed with its verdict. When more than one code applies, the lowest wins: 2 and 3 (conformance) before 4, and 4 (a condition is met) before 5 (a condition could not be judged). "Could not be judged" is a failure on purpose: a scan that could not look is not a scan that found nothing, so an air-gapped run with no vulnerability database never passes a vulnerability= gate by accident.

docs.title: Pin the scanner image version
docs.text:
Override the scanner image with SBOM_SCANNER_IMAGE.

SBOM_SCANNER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens:<version>" \
  ./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "MyApp" --version "1.0.0" --generate-only

docs.title: Windows: no outputs appear
docs.text: If the scan finishes but no output files show up, check that the folder you ran from is inside a Docker file-sharing path. Anything under your home directory (C:\Users\...) is shared by default in both Rancher Desktop and Docker Desktop. From an unshared location the container cannot write results to the host.

docs.title: Docker permission error (Linux/WSL2)
docs.text:
Got permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon

Does not apply on Windows/macOS with Rancher Desktop or Docker Desktop. Add your user to the docker group.

sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
newgrp docker

docs.title: Out of disk space
docs.text:
no space left on device

Prune the Docker cache. From a terminal:

docker system prune -f

With Rancher Desktop or Docker Desktop, the same cleanup is also available from the app's own Preferences screen.

docs.title: Interrupted build artifacts in the source tree
docs.text: A source scan (--target <dir>, the web UI's folder scan, or the desktop app) runs build steps (cargo generate-lockfile, go mod tidy, npm install, and the like) against the scanned tree, then restores it: every file a build step changed or added is put back or removed. If that scan ends by SIGKILL, an out-of-memory kill, or a host crash, the restore never runs and the changes stay. The next scan of that same source tree restores them first, before doing anything else, once it has confirmed the earlier scan's container is no longer running.

docs.title: Leftover output-folder artifacts on re-scan
docs.text: Re-scanning the same --project/--version reuses its output folder, however the earlier scan there ended. Before writing its own artifacts, the new scan removes any of BomLens's own files under that project/version that today's mode or options will not produce, so nothing from an earlier run with different options survives to be mistaken for this run's output. A file you placed in the folder yourself, or a different version's artifacts, is left alone.

docs.title: Anything else
docs.text:
1. Run the same command again and read the terminal output. The [WARN] and [ERROR] lines say what was skipped or what failed.
  2. Update the Docker image: docker pull ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens:latest.
  3. If it still fails, open a GitHub Issue with the command you ran and its terminal output. The issue form lists what it needs.

For how to use each mode, see the input scenarios guide; for the kinds of outputs, see the artifacts reference; for language detection, see supported ecosystems; to run scans in a pipeline, see CI/CD integration.

docs.title: Use the Docker image directly
docs.text: For everyday use we recommend the scan-sbom.sh script, which handles language detection, image selection, and volume mounts for you. This document explains how to call the image directly with docker run in environments where the script cannot live (CI runners, Kubernetes jobs, and so on).

docs.title: Images and tags
docs.text:
Image Purpose ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens Scanning and post-processing (canonical name) ghcr.io/sktelecom/sbom-generator, ghcr.io/sktelecom/sbom-scanner Aliases of the same image (former names, same digest) ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens-firmware Firmware analysis (includes GPL tools, opt-in) (legacy alias: sbom-scanner-firmware) ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens-deep-cve Bundles grype for deep CVE matching (opt-in). Used by the CLI's --deep-cve and by the web UI's Deep CVE matching toggle, both of which pull it automatically as a sibling container when it is not already the running image ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens-deep-license Bundles scancode for licence detection in the project's own files (opt-in). Used by the CLI's --deep-license for a source scan, pulled automatically. Carries LGPL components (7-Zip on linux/amd64, intbitset, chardet); the source for 7-Zip and intbitset is in the image under /usr/share/bomlens/sources/, and chardet ships as Python source ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens-aibom Generates an AI-model ML-BOM (opt-in, legacy alias: sbom-scanner-aibom). Used by --model/--model-file and the web UI's AI model tile, pulled automatically as a sibling container

latest and version tags are available. All published images (ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens, bomlens-firmware, bomlens-deep-cve, bomlens-deep-license, bomlens-aibom, and their aliases) support both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, so pulling any of them on an arm64 host (an Apple Silicon Mac, an Arm server) works natively. Images are signed with cosign before publishing.

On an arm64 host, do not force linux/amd64 (--platform linux/amd64 or DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM=linux/amd64): the image then runs under emulation, where syft in the firmware image can crash. A firmware scan tries a failed syft pass once more (not one that ran out of its time limit or was killed for memory), says in the log that it runs under emulation, and records generate as degraded in bomlens-result.json when the second try also fails.

docker pull ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens:latest

docs.title: What is in the image
docs.text:
It is a lightweight image (based on python 3.12 slim) without language toolchains. For source scans, transitive dependency resolution is handled by the script, which pulls per-language cdxgen images separately. See Architecture for the structure.

Tool Version Role syft v1.54.1 Scans images, binaries, and directories Trivy v0.75.0 Vulnerability report cosign v3.1.3 SBOM signing jq — SBOM normalization and notice generation ScanCode Toolkit 32.5.0 Precise license detection (included only in opt-in builds) SCANOSS 1.54.2 Identifies open source copied into C/C++ source (--identify-vendored) docker CLI 29.9.0 Starts a sibling cdxgen container when the web UI runs a source scan cdxgen 13.5.0 Model pedigree enrichment (bomlens-aibom image only)

Tool versions are pinned with ARG in docker/Dockerfile.

Every image also carries the NVD CPE index (cpe_match.sqlite, about 146 MB), built from the NVD data when the image is built. Firmware, root filesystem and binary scans with --security match the CPEs of components that have no package PURL against it, with no network (see How CVEs are matched). Building it clones the NVD data feeds from GitHub. When you build an image yourself where GitHub is not reachable, the build stops at that step and names --build-arg SBOM_CPE_INDEX=false, which leaves the index out; a firmware build does not accept it, so the firmware image always has the index.

docs.title: Running directly
docs.text: Select the analysis mode with the MODE environment variable. All examples below leave their outputs in the current directory and do not upload anything (UPLOAD_ENABLED=false).

docs.title: Analyze a Docker image
docs.text:
On Git Bash (Windows), MSYS rewrites both /var/run/docker.sock and the container-side /host-output into Windows paths before Docker ever sees them, silently breaking both mounts. MSYS_NO_PATHCONV and MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL below turn that rewriting off, and cygpath -m converts the host side back by hand instead (scripts/scan-sbom.sh uses the same pair for the same reason). WSL2, macOS and Linux shells don't rewrite paths and skip straight to the plain docker run line.

HOSTPATH="$(cygpath -m "$(pwd)" 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' docker run --rm \
  -v "$HOSTPATH":/host-output \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  -e MODE=IMAGE \
  -e TARGET_IMAGE="nginx:alpine" \
  -e UPLOAD_ENABLED=false \
  -e HOST_OUTPUT_DIR=/host-output \
  -e PROJECT_NAME="Nginx" \
  -e PROJECT_VERSION="alpine" \
  ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens:latest

docs.title: Analyze a binary file
docs.text:
HOSTPATH="$(cygpath -m "$(pwd)" 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' docker run --rm \
  -v "$HOSTPATH":/target \
  -v "$HOSTPATH":/host-output \
  -e MODE=BINARY \
  -e TARGET_FILE=/target/firmware.bin \
  -e UPLOAD_ENABLED=false \
  -e HOST_OUTPUT_DIR=/host-output \
  -e PROJECT_NAME="Firmware" \
  -e PROJECT_VERSION="1.0" \
  ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens:latest

docs.title: Analyze a source directory
docs.text:
HOSTPATH="$(cygpath -m "$(pwd)" 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' docker run --rm \
  -v "$HOSTPATH":/src \
  -v "$HOSTPATH":/host-output \
  -e MODE=SOURCE \
  -e UPLOAD_ENABLED=false \
  -e HOST_OUTPUT_DIR=/host-output \
  -e PROJECT_NAME="MyApp" \
  -e PROJECT_VERSION="1.0.0" \
  ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens:latest

In direct runs, SOURCE mode reads a lock file that covers the whole tree (a package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lock or gradle.lockfile, with no other manifest below the root) as it is, with no build and no Docker socket, and fills the licenses it lacks from the package registry; the SBOM records this as bomlens:detection. That is the form to use where there is no Docker to start a sibling container in, such as a CI job that runs this image as its job image. For any other tree, syft reads the package manifests inside the container, so it may only capture direct dependencies; if you need transitive dependencies there, use scan-sbom.sh, which routes to the per-language cdxgen images. Syft's manifest readers need a lockfile (package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml for Node, and the equivalent for other ecosystems) to resolve any of a project's declared dependencies; without one, direct-run SOURCE mode has nothing to read and the scan fails with guidance rather than reporting an empty result as complete.

docs.title: Notice and reports in one run
docs.text:
In direct runs, the notice and security reports are off by default. Turn on the following variables to get the same outputs as the CLI's --all.

HOSTPATH="$(cygpath -m "$(pwd)" 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' docker run --rm \
  -v "$HOSTPATH":/host-output \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  -e MODE=IMAGE \
  -e TARGET_IMAGE="nginx:alpine" \
  -e GENERATE_NOTICE=true \
  -e GENERATE_SECURITY=true \
  -e GENERATE_REPORT=true \
  -e UPLOAD_ENABLED=false \
  -e HOST_OUTPUT_DIR=/host-output \
  -e PROJECT_NAME="Nginx" \
  -e PROJECT_VERSION="alpine" \
  ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens:latest

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Required Default Description MODE No POSTPROCESS Analysis mode: SOURCE, IMAGE, BINARY, ROOTFS, FIRMWARE, ANALYZE, or PLAN (write the execution plan of a source scan, see Engine contract). Left unset, the container only post-processes an SBOM already sitting in the output directory — set it explicitly to actually scan something. PROJECT_NAME Yes — Project name PROJECT_VERSION Yes — Project version TARGET_IMAGE Per mode — Image for IMAGE mode. With the docker.sock mount it is read from the Docker daemon; without it, from the registry, or from an archive named with its scheme (docker-archive:, oci-archive:, oci-dir:) at a path mounted into the container SYFT_REGISTRY_AUTH_USERNAME, SYFT_REGISTRY_AUTH_PASSWORD, SYFT_REGISTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SYFT_REGISTRY_AUTH_AUTHORITY — — IMAGE mode: credentials for a private registry. A docker config file mounted and named in DOCKER_CONFIG works too. SYFT_REGISTRY_INSECURE_SKIP_TLS_VERIFY and SYFT_REGISTRY_INSECURE_USE_HTTP reach a registry with a self-signed certificate or plain HTTP. SYFT_PLATFORM picks the platform of a multi-platform image TARGET_FILE Per mode — File path for BINARY/FIRMWARE mode (path inside the container) TARGET_DIR Per mode — Directory path for ROOTFS mode UPLOAD_ENABLED — true If false, save locally without uploading (same as CLI --generate-only) HOST_OUTPUT_DIR — — Mounted path to copy the outputs to BOMLENS_STAGE1_EXIT, BOMLENS_STAGE1_OOM, BOMLENS_STAGE1_LOG, BOMLENS_STAGE1_REASON — — POSTPROCESS after a stage 1 you ran yourself: its exit code, true if it was killed for memory, and its log's file name in the output folder; or, instead of the last two, the reason already classified (oom, disk-space, network, cdxgen-crash, cdxgen-unavailable). Exit code 127 is read as cdxgen-unavailable: pass it for an unsupported plan, where no stage 1 ran. Stage 2 then falls back to a syft scan when stage 1 left no SBOM (see Engine contract) BOMLENS_EVENTS — — file or stderr: write progress events, one JSON object per line, to bomlens-events.jsonl in the output folder or to stderr (see Engine contract) BOMLENS_IMAGE_REF, BOMLENS_IMAGE_DIGEST — — The image reference and digest the caller ran, repeated in bomlens-result.json (see Engine contract) GENERATE_NOTICE — false Generate the open-source notice (CLI --notice) GENERATE_SECURITY — false Generate the Trivy security report (CLI --security) DEEP_LICENSE — false Detect licences in the project's own files with scancode (CLI --deep-license; needs scancode in the image) DEEP_LICENSE_MAX_FILES — 20000 DEEP_LICENSE: a tree with more of the project's own files than this is not scanned DEEP_LICENSE_TIMEOUT — 600 DEEP_LICENSE: seconds before scancode is stopped BOMLENS_DEEP_LICENSE_ALL — — DEEP_LICENSE: set 1 to scan dependency, build and tool folders too (left out by default) DETECTION — auto SOURCE mode only. auto reads a covering lock file statically and otherwise runs the build or syft path as before; static always reads statically; build never does (CLI --detection). Static detection fills missing licenses from the package registry, so auto builds under BYTE_STABLE=true or FETCH_LICENSE=false REACHABILITY — false Judge with govulncheck whether each Go advisory's code is reached (CLI --reachability): on the executable in BINARY mode; in SOURCE and POSTPROCESS, from the govulncheck output stage 1 left (the CLI hands stage 1 the image's govulncheck) GENERATE_REPORT — false Generate the open-source risk report (off in direct runs, unlike the CLI default) ENRICH_MAVEN_CPE — true Attach an NVD-matchable cpe:2.3 to maven components (derived from the groupId) so a CPE-aware engine can reach their NVD-only CVEs; unmapped groups get no CPE (skipped for AI SBOMs) ENRICH_GITHUB_CPE — true Attach an NVD-matchable cpe:2.3 to a small, hand-verified set of pkg:github/ components (source-repository-only coordinates, typical for large C/C++ projects with no package-manager ecosystem) so a CPE-aware engine can reach their NVD-only CVEs; anything not in the curated list gets no CPE (skipped for AI SBOMs) ENRICH_UPSTREAM_PURL — true For a firmware, root filesystem or binary scan, or an SBOM read from a Yocto build's records, set the purl of the upstream source repository (pkg:github/<owner>/<repo>@<tag>, pkg:sourceforge, pkg:gnu) on components that have no purl, a pkg:generic one or a pkg:opkg one, from the closed table in docker/lib/upstream-purl-map.json, or from a source download address that states a GitHub or GNU release. Any other component keeps its identifier ENRICH_INTERPRETER_CPE — true Attach an NVD-matchable cpe:2.3 to a small, hand-verified set of interpreter components (e.g. Python packaged as a conda or NuGet artifact) so a CPE-aware engine can reach their NVD-only CVEs; anything not in the curated list gets no CPE (skipped for AI SBOMs) SECURITY_NVD_VERIFY — false With --deep-cve: verify each grype nvd:cpe finding against the live NVD version range and drop out-of-range false positives (needs NVD_API_KEY + network; adds minutes). Off by default — findings are kept and flagged version-unverified NVD_API_KEY For SECURITY_NVD_VERIFY — NVD API key used by the deep-cve version filter; passed to the container by name only (never inlined) BOMLENS_OS_LICENSES — true IMAGE and ROOTFS modes: read the licenses of Debian packages with Trivy, which reads the license names, common-licenses references and license text in the copyright files syft leaves as a hash. It reads the image a second time; false turns it off (the hashes are still removed) BOMLENS_TRIVY_DB_MAX_AGE_DAYS — 7 With a Trivy database mounted at /trivy-db (read as it is, offline): the age in days past which the security step is recorded as degraded ENRICH_EOL — true Flag components past their upstream end-of-life from a bundled offline snapshot (skipped for AI SBOMs) ENRICH_MALICIOUS — true Flag components that are known-malicious packages (typosquats, hijacked accounts) from a bundled offline OSV snapshot. A separate signal from vulnerabilities: the response is removal and credential rotation, not an upgrade ENRICH_OS_CONTEXT — true Synthesize an operating-system component from distro package PURLs (rpm, deb, and apk). Trivy selects the distro vulnerability feed from that component, so without it the OS packages in a supplier SBOM or rootfs scan would get no OS CVE matches at all. No-op when the SBOM has no recognizable distro packages — including a distro Trivy carries no feed for, such as OpenWRT (skipped for AI SBOMs) ENRICH_DISTRO_SUPPLIER — true Fill supplier on an rpm, deb, or apk component with the distro project's name, read from the operating-system component ENRICH_OS_CONTEXT synthesizes. Left blank for a distro with no confirmed supplier name, an ambiguous (mixed-distro) SBOM, or a component that already carries a supplier (skipped for AI SBOMs) STALENESS_ENRICH — false Add deps.dev version currency (how many releases behind latest); needs network access ENRICH_HF_SECURITY — true AIBOM mode: read HuggingFace's per-file security scan results (ClamAV + picklescan) into the ML-BOM; metadata only, no file download API_KEY, API_URL For uploads — Upload credential and server URL. DT uses X-Api-Key; TRUSCA uses a Bearer token UPLOAD_TARGET — dependency-track Upload destination: dependency-track (DT-compatible) or trusca (native ingest, not DT-compatible) TRUSCA_PROJECT_ID When trusca — Target TRUSCA project id (UUID). Must already exist (no auto-create) TRUSCA_REF — main Ingest ref label TRUSCA_RELEASE — PROJECT_VERSION Ingest release label BOMLENS_MAVEN_FULL_GRAPH — — Maven source scans: set 1 to keep the full resolved graph instead of filtering to compile/runtime scope BOMLENS_NODE_FULL_GRAPH — — Node.js source scans: set 1 to keep the full dev-plus-production graph instead of the production-only set BOMLENS_ANDROID_FULL_GRAPH - - Android source scans (Android SDK image): set 1 to keep the full graph, build and test tooling included, instead of filtering to the release runtime classpath BOMLENS_PHP_FULL_GRAPH - - PHP (Composer) source scans: set 1 to keep the full require-plus-require-dev graph instead of filtering to the required set BOMLENS_KEEP_BUILD_OUTPUT — — Source scans: set 1 to leave the resolved tree in place. By default the scan restores the files its resolvers rewrote (go.mod, go.sum, Cargo.lock, Gemfile.lock, Package.resolved) and removes the build directories they created, so the scanned project is handed back as it was BOMLENS_PREP_TIMEOUT - 900 (1800 for Gradle/Android steps) Seconds a single dependency-resolution step (Cargo, Go, Bundler, pip, npm, pnpm, PHP Composer, Swift, Gradle/Android) is allowed to run before it is stopped and the scan moves on without it. Set to override both defaults for every step. A step that fails or times out is logged with its own output and recorded on the SBOM as bomlens:pipeline-step-failed; the scan itself still completes BOMLENS_CANCEL_GRACE — 30 Seconds a cancelled scan (CLI Ctrl+C, or the web UI's cancel button) gets to stop cleanly before it is force-stopped. Applies to the CLI and --ui; the desktop app always uses the default BOMLENS_INCLUDE_NON_SHIPPED - - Source scans: set 1 to keep the manifests under test, example, benchmark and demo folders, the GitHub Actions workflows in .github/workflows and the Gradle wrapper in gradle/wrapper, which are left out by default BOMLENS_INCLUDE_DEV_DEPENDENCIES - - Source scans: set 1 to keep the development-only components that are dropped by default (the ones cdxgen marks, and the gems a root Gemfile declares only in its development and test groups). The dropped components are recorded in bomlens:excluded-components BOMLENS_NO_COPYRIGHT - - Source scans: set 1 to skip filling npm, Python, Go and Rust component copyright from the installed packages' license files BOMLENS_NO_CARGO_LICENSE - - Source scans: set 1 to skip filling Rust component licenses from cargo metadata (FETCH_LICENSE=false on the command line skips it too) CYCLONEDX_SPEC_VERSION — 1.6 CycloneDX version of the generated SBOM, 1.6 or 1.7 (the CLI's --spec-version). AI model and dataset SBOMs are always 1.7. Any other value stops the run CYCLONEDX_SPEC_VERSIONS — 1.3 1.4 1.5 1.6 1.7 Accepted CycloneDX spec versions for the conformance check (space-separated); overrides the default range AI_CYCLONEDX_SPEC_VERSIONS — 1.3 1.4 1.5 1.6 1.7 Accepted CycloneDX versions for AI SBOMs (ML-BOM); always includes 1.7, the version the AIBOM toolchain emits SPDX_SPEC_VERSIONS — SPDX-2.2 SPDX-2.3 Accepted SPDX spec versions for the conformance check PURL_MIN_PCT — 90 Conformance check: minimum percentage of components with a PURL (mandatory check). Applies to a --deep-cve scan too, CLI or web UI LICENSE_MIN_PCT — 80 Conformance check: minimum percentage of components with a license (recommended, warn only). Applies to a --deep-cve scan too, CLI or web UI HASH_MIN_PCT — 50 Conformance check: minimum percentage of components with a hash (recommended, warn only). Applies to a --deep-cve scan too, CLI or web UI FIELD_MIN_PCT — 80 Conformance check: minimum percentage coverage for advisory per-component regulatory fields. Applies to a --deep-cve scan too, CLI or web UI PURL_TYPES_FILE — docker/lib/purl-types.json Conformance check: the purl-spec type data that says which types exist and which of them require a namespace NS_ADVISORY_TYPES — golang huggingface Conformance check: types whose missing namespace is reported on the advisory row instead of failing the SBOM (space-separated) LICENSE_REGISTRY — false The script's --license-registry: look up missing licences, and check a single strong-copyleft or non-commercial licence, in the package registry (deps.dev). Uses the network LICENSE_REGISTRY_VERIFY — GPL, AGPL, SSPL-1.0, BUSL-1.1 and CC-BY-NC ids SPDX ids whose single occurrence is checked against the registry, space- or comma-separated LICENSE_REGISTRY_BUDGET — 240 Seconds the lookups may take in total. Components it does not reach are left as they were, and the step is recorded as degraded LICENSE_REGISTRY_API — https://api.deps.dev/v3 Base URL of a server that answers the deps.dev v3 version lookup, for a network that reaches the registries only through its own mirror or proxy. When nothing answers, the components stay as they were and the step is recorded as degraded (unavailable) PURL_RESOLVE — false --analyze only (the script's --resolve-purl): look each identifier up in its package repository (deps.dev) and add the answer to the conformance check report as an advisory row. Uses the network PURL_RESOLVE_IGNORE — — Namespace prefixes to leave out of that lookup, space- or comma-separated. Use it for namespaces published only to an internal repository, which cannot be told apart from a wrong identifier PURL_RESOLVE_BUDGET — 240 Seconds the lookup may take in total. Identifiers it does not reach are reported as unchecked, never as missing

TRUSCA's (formerly TrustedOSS Portal) native ingest endpoint (POST /v1/projects/{id}/sbom-ingest, Bearer auth) is not Dependency-Track compatible. To push to a regular Dependency-Track server, keep UPLOAD_TARGET=dependency-track (the default).

For the full mapping between CLI flags and environment variables, see the flag mapping in Architecture.

docs.title: Supported ecosystems
docs.text:
A hands-on guide using the per-language example projects under examples/. Run each example to see the SBOM output right away.

How BomLens runs each ecosystem's build tool, and how it narrows the result to what ships, is explained in How dependencies are resolved.

docs.title: Example directory structure
docs.text:
examples/
├── java-maven/      # Java + Maven
├── java-gradle/     # Java + Gradle
├── nodejs/          # Node.js + npm
├── python/          # Python + pip / Poetry
├── go/              # Go modules
├── ruby/            # Ruby + Bundler
├── php/             # PHP + Composer
├── rust/            # Rust + Cargo
├── dotnet/          # .NET + NuGet
├── swift/           # Swift + SPM (Swift Package Manager)
├── modelica/        # Modelica (.mo) uses() declarations
└── docker/          # Docker image analysis

docs.title: Common run steps
docs.text:
Every source-code example runs the same way from the repository root: point --target at the example folder and pick a project name. The results are saved in a {Project}_{Version}/ subfolder. For the Node.js example:

# 1. Generate the SBOM (from the repository root)
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "NodeExample" --version "1.0.0" --target examples/nodejs --generate-only

# 2. Check the result
jq '.components | length' NodeExample_1.0.0/NodeExample_1.0.0_bom.json

By default a source scan leaves out the manifests under test, fixture, example, benchmark and demo folders (test, tests, spec, fixtures, testdata, __tests__, e2e, example, examples, sample, samples, bench, benches, benchmark, benchmarks, demo, demos, playground), the GitHub Actions workflows in .github/workflows and the Gradle wrapper in gradle/wrapper (its gradle-wrapper.jar), because none of them ship with the product. The SBOM records the patterns in the bomlens:excluded-paths property and the files it left out in bomlens:excluded-manifests. To include them, set BOMLENS_INCLUDE_NON_SHIPPED=1 (Docker image environment variables).

A source scan also drops the development-only components that cdxgen marks: npm, pnpm, yarn and bun development packages, uv and Poetry dependency groups other than main, Cargo dev-dependencies, and sbt, Crystal and Gleam development dependencies. For Ruby, BomLens reads the Gemfile groups itself (see Ruby). When cdxgen gives a component the same marker more than once, the component counts as development-only only if every value is a development one. A marked component, and a dependency that only marked components reach, is dropped only when nothing else in the dependency graph reaches it: every unmarked component keeps what it depends on, including a component the root does not reach, and a workspace member keeps its own dependencies, so the dev-dependencies of a Cargo workspace member crate and the dependency groups of a uv workspace member stay. npm development packages are the exception: cdxgen 13.5.0 sets that marker over the whole workspace, so a package that carries it is one no member's production dependencies reach, and it is dropped even when a member lists it. The SBOM records the dropped components in the bomlens:excluded-components property. To keep them, set BOMLENS_INCLUDE_DEV_DEPENDENCIES=1 (Docker image environment variables). The language sections below say what this means for each ecosystem.

For npm, Python (pip), Go and Rust (Cargo) packages, a source scan also fills each component's copyright from the license files the installed package ships (LICENSE, LICENCE, COPYING, NOTICE, COPYRIGHT), so the NOTICE can print an attribution line. Only a line that begins with Copyright followed directly by (c), the copyright sign, a year or by (or with (c) or the sign followed by a year), and that names a holder, is used. A notice with no year, such as Copyright Acme, Inc., is not taken. Lines come from the package's own folder only (its .dist-info folder for Python; for Go the folder go list reports, which is the module cache, the replacement's folder for a replaced module, or vendor/; for Rust the folder cargo metadata reports, which is the cargo registry, a git checkout or a path dependency), at most 6 files, the first 64 KiB and 400 lines of each, and at most 5 statements per component, joined with ;. Lines that are an unfilled template (<year>, [fullname]) or the text of a license itself (for example the Free Software Foundation's own line in a GNU license) are skipped, and so are files that link outside the package. A component that already has a copyright is not changed, a package with no such line stays empty, and each value set carries the property bomlens:copyrightSource. Set BOMLENS_NO_COPYRIGHT=1 to turn this off. Java (Maven) is not covered: Maven downloads jar files rather than source folders, so the license files of a dependency are not on disk to read. A replaced Go module carries the statement of the code that is actually built, which can be a different version from the one the component names. The scanned project's own Go module and Rust workspace crates are not filled. The Rust step reads the crate sources that are already on disk and never goes to the network for them, so with FETCH_LICENSE=false or --byte-stable a crate that was not downloaded stays empty. A Go or Rust component whose folder is not on disk, for example because the download failed, stays empty. When no folder of an ecosystem could be listed at all, the SBOM records it in the bomlens:copyrightUnread metadata property (golang, cargo), so that a missing copyright can be told from a step that did not run.

The sections below give the ready-to-paste command for each language.

docs.title: Java (Maven)
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "JavaMavenExample" --version "1.0.0" --target examples/java-maven --generate-only

Detected file: pom.xml

<!-- example pom.xml -->
<dependencies>
  <dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
    <version>3.2.0</version>
  </dependency>
</dependencies>

Note: cdxgen resolves the whole build graph, so BomLens filters the SBOM to the deployable set — compile and runtime scope — and drops the test and provided toolchain (JUnit, Lombok, and the like) so the result reflects what ships rather than the full build. To keep the complete resolved graph instead, set BOMLENS_MAVEN_FULL_GRAPH=1 (Docker image environment variables). A runtime dependency declared with <optional>true</optional> is dropped as well, because cdxgen gives it the same tag as a test-scope one. A multi-module reactor can carry modules that never get deployed alongside the ones that do: a demo, or a module the project itself excludes from mvn deploy (maven-deploy-plugin's skip resolving to true, however it is set). Such a module's own component is left out. A dependency only that module needs is left out too, but only when no deployed module in the same reactor declares it at any scope (a deployed module's own provided or test declaration of it, not just a compile/runtime one, is enough to keep it, since the SBOM's dependency graph does not record which scope each edge represents). BOMLENS_MAVEN_FULL_GRAPH=1 keeps everything this leaves out. The excluded modules and the components dropped because of them are recorded on the SBOM as bomlens:excluded-modules and bomlens:excluded-components.

Note: cdxgen reads a Maven component's license from its own pom.xml only, so one that declares no <licenses> and relies on Maven's own inheritance from a parent POM comes through with none. BomLens now walks that parent chain itself (the reactor's own modules, then the local repository for a parent outside it) and fills the license from the first ancestor that declares one, leaving the component untouched if none do or if it already carries a license. The filled component is recorded with a bomlens:licenseSource property set to parent POM.

Note: dependency and license resolution need the container to reach Maven Central, or your mirror. When it cannot, the result holds only the dependencies written in pom.xml, with no transitive dependencies and no licenses, and the scan finishes without a warning. If the component count is far below what you expect, check network access first.

docs.title: Java (Gradle)
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "JavaGradleExample" --version "1.0.0" --target examples/java-gradle --generate-only

Detected file: build.gradle or build.gradle.kts

Note: as with Maven, resolution needs the container to reach Maven Central, or your mirror. When it cannot, the result can hold only the direct dependencies, with no licenses. If the component count is far below what you expect, check network access first.

docs.title: Android
docs.text:
Detected when the project has a Gradle root (settings.gradle[.kts] or build.gradle[.kts] at the root) and shows a sign of the Android Gradle plugin: the plugin id in the version catalog (gradle/libs.versions.toml), the plugin id or a catalog alias in a build script (root or app/), a Kotlin DSL namespace declaration, or an AndroidManifest.xml a few levels down. A manifest with no Gradle root does not count on its own, which also keeps a .NET MAUI app's Platforms/Android/AndroidManifest.xml from being misread as an Android project.

Android needs an SDK platform image BomLens does not publish: the Android SDK it contains is not open source, and Google's terms do not allow redistributing it, so the image is built locally instead. The project's compileSdk/compileSdkVersion picks the API level (34 if none is found); the scan then looks for bomlens-android-sdk<API>:latest, and if it is missing, prints the build command instead of failing on a missing image:

docker build --build-arg ANDROID_API=<API> -t bomlens-android-sdk<API> docker/android

Building it means accepting Google's SDK terms yourself. Set ANDROID_IMAGE_PREFIX to use an image built elsewhere.

Note: images published under ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens-android-sdk<API> up to v1.9.0 still work for scans on that release line, but nothing new is pushed to them; a current scan needs a locally built image.

docs.title: Node.js
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "NodeExample" --version "1.0.0" --target examples/nodejs --generate-only

Detected file: package.json + package-lock.json (or yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml)

Note: a lock file pins the exact installed versions. Dependencies are still captured from package.json without one, but committing a lock file makes the result reproducible.

Note: the SBOM is filtered to the production dependency set, so devDependencies are dropped and the result reflects what ships. To keep the full dev-plus-production graph instead, set BOMLENS_NODE_FULL_GRAPH=1 (Docker image environment variables).

Note: an npm workspace member registered in package-lock.json survives the file-level exclusion above even when its own directory sits under an excluded tree, because cdxgen reads package-lock.json directly. Such a member's own component is left out too, along with a dependency only that member needs, unless a kept member reaches it as well. BOMLENS_INCLUDE_NON_SHIPPED=1 (the same switch as the file-level exclusion above) keeps everything this leaves out. The excluded members and the components dropped because of them are recorded on the SBOM as bomlens:excluded-members and bomlens:excluded-components. A yarn workspace member is not caught the same way yet.

Note: on top of the production filter, a component cdxgen marks as a development package (npm, pnpm, yarn or bun) is dropped when no production dependency path reaches it, together with what only it reaches. This also covers a pnpm workspace, which the production filter does not read. A package a production dependency also uses stays. BOMLENS_NODE_FULL_GRAPH=1 or BOMLENS_INCLUDE_DEV_DEPENDENCIES=1 keeps these too.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "PythonExample" --version "1.0.0" --target examples/python --generate-only

Detected file: requirements.txt, or pyproject.toml + poetry.lock

Note: a Poetry project without poetry.lock is scanned from the exact pins in [tool.poetry.dependencies] (requests = "2.31.0"); ranges such as ^2.0 and path or git entries are left out. The pins are linked from the project and come with their own dependencies; when some entries were left out, or the dependencies could not be resolved (no network), the SBOM declares its dependency graph incomplete. Pin versions with == or commit a lock file such as poetry.lock. Without them the SBOM lists the versions available at scan time, not the ones you run. The bundled example pins its versions, and every component carries a license.

Note: with uv (uv.lock) or Poetry, a component cdxgen places only in dependency groups other than main, such as dev or test, is dropped when no production dependency path reaches it, together with what only it reaches. A package the production dependencies also use stays, and so does a package that any pyproject.toml in the project names in its [project] dependencies or optional-dependencies or in [tool.poetry.dependencies], even when a dependency group lists it too. BomLens reads these files with a small reader of its own: when the scan root has no pyproject.toml, or a file uses a form the reader does not follow (for example dynamic = ["dependencies"]), no Python package is dropped and the build log says so. The same happens when a requirements*.txt, setup.py, setup.cfg or Pipfile is in the project outside vendor and the folders a source scan leaves out by default (see above), since it may declare production dependencies the reader does not see. The search goes 8 folders deep and skips vendor, node_modules, .git and virtual environments (.venv, venv); a deeper folder outside those and the non-shipped folders also means no Python package is dropped.

docs.title: Go
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "GoExample" --version "1.0.0" --target examples/go --generate-only

Detected file: go.mod + go.sum

Note: go.sum is required for accurate version hashes. Run go mod tidy first, then try again.

docs.title: Ruby
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "RubyExample" --version "1.0.0" --target examples/ruby --generate-only

Detected file: Gemfile.lock

Note: with no Gemfile.lock committed, BomLens runs bundle lock before scanning. Commit the lock file so the SBOM matches what you deploy.

Note: cdxgen does not mark Bundler groups, so BomLens reads the Gemfile at the scan root itself. A gem declared only in the development and test groups (in a group ... do block or with a group: or groups: option) is dropped, along with what only those gems need, unless a production gem also needs it. The Gemfile is read conservatively: a condition, gemspec, eval_gemfile, a declaration over several lines or any other line the reader does not recognise, or a Gemfile.lock that names a gem the Gemfile does not, leaves every gem in place, and the log says Gemfile groups not read. So does another Gemfile or Gemfile.lock below the scan root, or a .gemspec file anywhere in the project, since it may declare the same gems for production. That search goes 8 folders deep and skips vendor (with the installed gems in vendor/bundle), node_modules, .git, .venv and venv; a deeper folder outside those also leaves every gem in place.

docs.title: PHP
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "PHPExample" --version "1.0.0" --target examples/php --generate-only

Detected file: composer.lock

Note: with no composer.lock committed, BomLens resolves one itself (composer update --no-dev, on a copy of composer.json without require-dev and config.lock, with platform requirements ignored) before scanning, the same as it does for Ruby's Gemfile.lock. Your composer.json is put back afterwards. A dependency version that needs a newer PHP than the project declares can be picked, because the PHP version is not enforced. cdxgen already tags each composer component with its resolved scope (require becomes required, require-dev becomes optional), so BomLens filters the SBOM to the required set, the same way it does for Maven. To keep the full require-plus-require-dev graph instead, set BOMLENS_PHP_FULL_GRAPH=1 (Docker image environment variables).

docs.title: Rust
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "RustExample" --version "1.0.0" --target examples/rust --generate-only

Detected file: Cargo.lock

Note: cdxgen reads only Cargo.lock, which carries no licenses, so BomLens fills them from cargo metadata, which reads each crate's own manifest (your own workspace crates included). The container needs a route to the crate registry (crates.io or your mirror) for this. Without one, the SBOM records a license for almost no Cargo packages and the notice file built from the scan is nearly empty. The scan then records the step cargo-license-metadata as failed on the SBOM, which the result screen and the conformance check report show, and the log says could not read crate licenses. A crate that declares its license only as a file (license-file) stays without one. Alternatives such as MIT OR Apache-2.0 are written in a fixed order, so the same pair is one entry in the notice however a crate spells it, and a value that is not an SPDX expression is kept as a plain license name. The bundled example lists 147 libraries and 146 of them carry a license. BOMLENS_NO_CARGO_LICENSE=1 turns this off, and so does FETCH_LICENSE=false on the command line. --deep-license does not help here: it scans your own source files, not the dependencies, and writes a separate report.

Note: a Cargo workspace member registered in Cargo.lock survives the file-level exclusion above even when its own directory sits under an excluded tree, because cdxgen reads Cargo.lock directly. Such a member's own component is left out too, along with a dependency only that member needs, unless a kept member reaches it as well (any way at all). BOMLENS_INCLUDE_NON_SHIPPED=1 (the same switch as the file-level exclusion above) keeps everything this leaves out. The excluded members and the components dropped because of them are recorded on the SBOM as bomlens:excluded-members and bomlens:excluded-components.

Note: a crate cdxgen marks only as a dev-dependency ([dev-dependencies]) is dropped when no production dependency path reaches it, together with what only it reaches. A crate the production dependencies also use stays, and so does one listed in both [dependencies] and [dev-dependencies]. cdxgen sets this marker with or without a committed Cargo.lock, since BomLens resolves one when it is missing. In a workspace, the dev-dependencies of a member crate stay, because what a member depends on is kept whatever its marker; only the dev-dependencies of the root package can be dropped.

docs.title: .NET
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "DotNetExample" --version "1.0.0" --target examples/dotnet --generate-only

Detected files: *.csproj, *.fsproj, *.sln or *.slnx, at the root or in folders up to three levels below it. packages.lock.json is read when present

Note: detection needs a project or solution file. packages.lock.json is not required, but committing one (dotnet restore --use-lock-file) pins the resolved versions so the SBOM is reproducible.

docs.title: Swift / iOS
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "SwiftExample" --version "1.0.0" --target examples/swift --generate-only

Detected files: Package.swift (+ Package.resolved) for Swift Package Manager, or Podfile.lock for CocoaPods.

Dependencies are read from the committed lockfiles, so include them in the scan:

  • Swift Package Manager: Package.resolved (run swift package resolve first if it is missing).
  • CocoaPods: Podfile.lock (produced by pod install). BomLens parses it directly, so the scanning machine needs neither macOS nor a CocoaPods install.

Note: UIKit and other Xcode-driven platform dependencies require macOS and are not resolved in the Linux scanner.

Note: the bundled example lists 6 components, of which 5 carry a PURL (83%) and 2 a license (33%). Both are below the default thresholds of the conformance checks: the PURL check fails and the license check warns. The two resolved packages (swift-argument-parser, swift-log) have a PURL and a license. The rest are the package itself and the platform modules it imports (Foundation, XCTest, dispatch), which have no license to declare. BomLens drops the versionless duplicates of a resolved package that the import scan adds, so a package is counted once.

docs.title: Modelica
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "ModelicaExample" --version "1.0.0" --target examples/modelica --generate-only

Detected files: *.mo

cdxgen has no Modelica cataloger, so the usual package-manager approach reads no dependencies. Instead, BomLens parses the annotation(uses(...)) block a .mo package declares directly, picking up each library named there together with its version. A uses() declaration carries only a name and a version, so a license comes from BomLens's own table of known libraries (docker/lib/modelica-library-map.json), not from your project. The table records the license read from each library's upstream license file (Modelica Standard Library 3.2.3 and later: BSD-3-Clause; Buildings 13.0.0 and later: BSD-3-Clause-LBNL). Both libraries in the bundled example get a license this way (2 of 2), recorded with the property bomlens:licenseSource = modelica-library-map. A library outside the table, or a version older than the recorded one, has no license.

annotation(uses(Modelica(version="4.0.0"), Buildings(version="13.0.0")));

Note: only the libraries declared directly in uses() are identified. Modelica has no lockfile, so transitive dependencies are not resolved, and the model's own internal structure (its components, parameters, connections) is not open-source dependency data, so it is left out.

docs.title: Conda
docs.text:
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh --project "CondaExample" --version "1.0.0" --target . --generate-only

Detected files: environment.yml or environment.yaml at the root of the scanned folder.

cdxgen has no Conda cataloger, so BomLens reads the dependencies: list of the environment file itself. Each conda entry becomes a pkg:conda/... component, and each entry under a pip: item becomes a pkg:pypi/... component.

dependencies:
  - python=3.11
  - numpy=1.26.4
  - pip:
    - requests==2.31.0

When the file is read successfully, BomLens turns off cdxgen's Python step for that scan. Otherwise a setup.py or requirements.txt elsewhere in the tree would replace the environment file as the source of truth.

Note: only the two-level layout shown above is recognized, with dependencies: at the left edge, entries indented by two spaces and pip: items by four. A file that uses another layout (a different indent width, a flow-style list, a tab) is not partly read. It is skipped as a whole and cdxgen's Python step runs as before. An entry with no version or only a range such as >=1.0 does not name a version, so it is recorded without a version or PURL and carries the property bomlens:versionUnpinned. Editable and VCS installs under pip: are left out.

docs.title: Docker image analysis
docs.text:
Run Docker image analysis from the project root.

# Analyze a public image
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh \
  --project "NginxSBOM" \
  --version "1.25" \
  --target "nginx:1.25-alpine" \
  --generate-only

# Ubuntu-based image
./scripts/scan-sbom.sh \
  --project "UbuntuSBOM" \
  --version "22.04" \
  --target "ubuntu:22.04" \
  --generate-only

Note: --target takes an image name or an image tar here. Pointing it at the examples/docker folder, which holds no dependency manifest, finds no components.

docs.title: Files required for detection
docs.text:
If source analysis finds no dependencies, check for the lock file below.

Language Required file Java (Maven) pom.xml Java (Gradle) build.gradle or build.gradle.kts Node.js package.json + package-lock.json or yarn.lock Python requirements.txt or pyproject.toml + poetry.lock Go go.mod + go.sum Conda environment.yml or environment.yaml (root folder) Rust Cargo.lock Ruby Gemfile.lock PHP composer.lock .NET *.csproj, *.fsproj, *.sln or *.slnx (root or up to three folders down); packages.lock.json is optional Swift Package.swift (+ Package.resolved) or Podfile.lock Modelica a .mo file with an annotation(uses(...)) block Android a Gradle root (settings.gradle[.kts] or build.gradle[.kts]) plus a sign of the Android Gradle plugin, see Android Docker image no file: pass an image name or an image tar as --target

docs.title: Results on the bundled examples
docs.text:
The bundled examples were scanned on 2026-09-21 with BomLens 1.12.0 and the source-scan changes made after it. The table counts software components only. The Copyright column is the share of components whose copyright is filled (see above); Ruby, PHP, .NET, Swift and Modelica are not covered. The default conformance thresholds are 90% for PURL and 80% for license.

Example Components PURL License Copyright Node.js 120 100% 100% 95% Python 39 100% 100% 82% Go 19 100% 100% 94% Ruby 9 100% 100% 0% PHP 16 100% 100% 0% .NET 70 100% 98% 0% Rust 157 100% 99% 83% Swift 6 83% 33% 0% Modelica 2 100% 100% 0%

Java (Maven), Java (Gradle) and Docker are not in the table. The Java scans could not be measured on the network used, where Maven Central did not serve artifacts (see the notes above). The Docker example is an image-scan example and finds nothing when scanned as a folder. These are results on small example projects, not a forecast for yours: a real project's coverage depends on its own dependencies.

docs.text:
The PURL (Package URL) format in the generated SBOM differs by language.

Language PURL example Java pkg:maven/org.springframework.boot/spring-boot@3.2.0 Node.js pkg:npm/express@4.18.2 Python pkg:pypi/requests@2.31.0 Go pkg:golang/github.com/gin-gonic/gin@v1.9.1 Rust pkg:cargo/serde@1.0.193 Ruby pkg:gem/rails@7.1.2 PHP pkg:composer/laravel/laravel@10.3.3 .NET pkg:nuget/Newtonsoft.Json@13.0.3 Swift pkg:swift/github.com/apple/swift-log@1.5.0 Docker (OS packages) pkg:deb/debian/curl@7.88.1

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If you run into trouble running an example, see the troubleshooting section of the CLI reference.

Related: First scan | CLI reference

docs.title: Engine contract
docs.text:
A program that runs the BomLens image as its scan engine reads bomlens-result.json, written to the output folder by every scan. It says how the run ended, which steps ran, were turned off, could not run or failed, and which file in the folder plays which role, so the program does not parse the log or guess file names.

The format is checked against schemas/engine-result-1.json by tests/test-engine-contract.sh in CI. This page describes contract version 1.3.0.

docs.title: The file
docs.text:
bomlens-result.json has a fixed name, so give each scan its own output folder. A manifest left in the folder by an earlier run is removed when the run starts, before anything else is checked, and the new one is written when the run ends, also when it stops early on an error. A folder with no manifest after the run means the engine was killed before it could write one.

The scan's exit code is unchanged by the contract. A run that produced its SBOM exits 0 even when a step failed along the way; the manifest is where that failure is reported. There are two exceptions. A --component-versions file that is refused: every file is still written, and the run exits 1, since the versions it was given were not applied. And a --components file (or sbom-declared.cdx.json) that is refused: unlike --component-versions, the run stops at once, before the SBOM is normalized, signed or uploaded, and exits 1, since an SBOM without the declared components is not the one that was asked for. The SBOM written up to that point is renamed to {Project}_{Version}_bom.refused.json, so a step that picks up _bom.json cannot take the incomplete one.

Field Meaning contract name is bomlens-engine, version the contract version (semantic versioning, separate from the BomLens version) engine version is the BomLens version built into the image. image and image_digest repeat BOMLENS_IMAGE_REF and BOMLENS_IMAGE_DIGEST when the caller passes them; the image cannot see its own reference input kind (source, image, sbom, binary, rootfs, firmware, ai-model, dataset), the MODE it ran in, target (the image reference for an image scan; paths are not recorded), and for an image scan image (below) run status, reason, started_at, ended_at (UTC), exit_code steps[] one entry per step, in the order they were recorded; a step is recorded when it ends (below) tools tool name and version: the generator recorded in the SBOM, syft, and Trivy when the vulnerability scan ran engines the vulnerability engines whose results this run produced (trivy, grype, cve-bin-tool, yocto) data_sources.trivy_db the Trivy database's schema version, updated_at and downloaded_at, when the vulnerability scan ran outputs[] role, path (relative to the output folder), sha256 and bytes of each file the run wrote

docs.title: Run status
docs.text:
run.status When succeeded exit code 0, and every recorded step ok, disabled, or skipped because it had nothing to read (no_input) succeeded_degraded exit code 0, and at least one step failed or degraded, or skipped for any other reason (a step that was asked for and could not run: its tool not installed, its input over a limit, its image unavailable). The SBOM is valid; read steps[] to decide whether the failed step matters to you failed the run exited with a non-zero code (reason is exit_code) cancelled the run was stopped by a signal (exit code 130 or 143)

A failed vulnerability scan never yields succeeded. Trivy writes an empty result with a ScanError when its database cannot be read; the manifest reports that as scan-security failed, with Trivy's message in detail, so "no vulnerabilities" and "the scan did not run" stay apart.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
Every step that applies to the scan's mode is recorded, also when it did not run. A step that does not apply to the mode at all (CPE enrichment of an AI model) is left out.

status Meaning ok ran and completed degraded ran, but with less than it needed (for example, the offline end-of-life data was missing) failed ran and failed; the SBOM is still written. Most post-process steps also add their name to the SBOM's bomlens:pipeline-step-failed property; the manifest is the complete record skipped could not run: its tool is not in the image, or its input is missing disabled a setting turned it off reason Meaning failed the step returned an error timeout the step ran out of time not_installed the tool it needs is not in this image too_large the input was over the step's size limit fallback a simpler method was used instead (the SBOM came from the manifest-only fallback, direct dependencies only, or a Poetry project with no poetry.lock was resolved only in part: ranged or table dependencies left out, or the pins' own dependencies not resolved), or the step ran without the image it needs (--deep-license when the scancode image could not be pulled, --deep-cve when the grype image could not be pulled) unavailable the data the step reads was not available budget_exhausted the step stopped at its work limit no_input there was nothing for the step to read (no source tree, no signing key) no_components the source declares dependencies (a manifest or lock file lists some) but the SBOM has no component; detail names the manifests and the resolver steps that failed, if any. Recorded on generate

No step reports budget_exhausted yet; it is reserved for a work limit a later release records.

Each step also has stage (1 for the SBOM a language image generated before this container started, 2 otherwise), started_at, ended_at, an optional detail of up to 500 characters, and for some steps counts (generate records components, and unresolved when it left out packages the generator saw but could not name, which detail then says). In POSTPROCESS mode generate also has input_fingerprint, reused, reuse_unsafe and, after an execution plan, plan_mismatch (see Input fingerprint).

Step What it does plan write the execution plan (MODE=PLAN, below) generate produce the SBOM (stage 1 for a source scan, where the language image ran first); degraded (failed) when a step inside generation failed (a syft pass of a firmware scan, a resolver step of a source scan) and recorded itself only in the SBOM's bomlens:pipeline-step-failed, with those steps named in detail; when a firmware syft pass is among them and the amd64 image ran under emulation on an ARM host, detail also says so, and on an arm64 host names the linux/arm64 image to use instead. The label of a post-process step (a step of its own in this table) is never counted here, even from an SBOM an earlier run left os-licenses an image or root filesystem scan: the licenses of Debian packages from Trivy, which reads the license names, common-licenses references and license text in the copyright files syft leaves as a hash; counts gives replaced and hashes_dropped, degraded (unavailable) when Trivy could not read the target or gave no Debian package a license, skipped (not_installed) without Trivy, disabled with BOMLENS_OS_LICENSES=false vendored identify open source copied into the sources (--identify-vendored) suggest-vendored suggest that identification when a C/C++ project scanned near-empty cocoapods add CocoaPods dependencies from Podfile.lock stamp-metadata set the root component to the project name and version; for an SBOM read from a Yocto build directory, give the image a bom-ref, the version when the build wrote none, the --license and an edge to every installed package; the run stops if this fails declared-components a source scan: add the components listed in --components files or sbom-declared.cdx.json; a Yocto build: apply the --components files to the packages of each recipe named in bomlens:yocto-recipe; recorded only when there is a file to read, with the number of components marked bomlens:declared in counts; failed when a file is refused, with the reason in detail, and the run then exits 1 docmeta record the document's author, tool and lifecycle phase license-registry ask the package registry for missing licences and check a single strong-copyleft or non-commercial one (--license-registry); counts gives candidates, filled, superseded, confirmed, no_answer, not_found, non_standard, lookup_failed, budget_reached component-versions a firmware, root filesystem or binary scan: fill the versions given with --component-versions, record the reasons given as bomlens:versionReason, and write the components still missing a version and a reason to _component-versions.template.csv; failed when the file is refused, with the reason in detail, and the run then exits 1 normalize normalize licences, PURLs and duplicates enrich-cpe add CPE identifiers upstream-purl a firmware, root filesystem or binary scan, or the records of a Yocto build: set the upstream source repository purl from the mapping table; disabled with ENRICH_UPSTREAM_PURL=false enrich-os-context record the operating system packages' distribution enrich-distro-supplier record the distribution as the OS packages' supplier enrich-maven-cpe add CPEs for Maven components enrich-github-cpe add CPEs for components named by GitHub repository enrich-interpreter-cpe add CPEs for language runtimes enrich-eol mark end-of-life versions (offline data) enrich-malicious mark known malicious packages (offline data) enrich-staleness measure how far behind each version is (opt-in, online) declared-sources apply the dataset sources an AI declaration names declared-service apply the AI service an AI declaration describes assess-ai-risk assess the AI model's risk resolve-purl look each PURL up in its package repository (--resolve-purl) describe-input record the supplier SBOM's own format and tool (--analyze) conformance check the SBOM against the minimum elements deep-license detect licences in the source files with scancode (--deep-license) source-file-tree record the scanned tree's file list source-snapshot keep the scanned files' content for the file viewer generate-notice write the open source notice match-cpe a firmware, root filesystem or binary scan, or a Yocto SPDX 2.2 archive, with --security: match the CPEs of components that have no package PURL against the NVD CPE index bundled in the image; counts gives offered, components and cves, skipped (not_installed) in an image without the index, disabled without --security or with CVE_BIN_TOOL_MODE=components-only reachability a Go source or Go executable scan: judge with govulncheck whether the code each Go advisory names is reached (--reachability, REACHABILITY=true); counts gives exploitable, not_affected and components; skipped (unavailable) when the Go vulnerability database could not be read, (no_input) when the SBOM has no Go component or stage 1 left no govulncheck output for this run, (too_large) when the source tree has more than 20 Go modules, degraded (unavailable) when a Go module builds for none of GOOS linux, darwin and windows and is not judged, (not_installed) in an image without govulncheck; disabled without the option scan-security match vulnerabilities with Trivy deep-cve with --security: match the components that carry a CPE, and the extra CPEs in bomlens:cpeAlternates, against NVD with grype (--deep-cve, the deep-cve image); skipped (not_installed) when asked for in an image without grype, skipped (fallback) when the CLI ran it without the deep-cve image, because that image could not be pulled or the scanner image is a local build, a version before 1.13.2 or not a BomLens image name (detail says which; a kept image that has grype, built with SBOM_DEEP_CVE=true, runs the match and records its real outcome), disabled when not asked for, without --security, and in a firmware or AI model scan generate-risk-report write the risk report model-security check an AI model file for unsafe content verify-weights check that a model's published weights match their hashes enrich-aibom add details read from the model's hub page sign sign the SBOM with cosign (--sign)

docs.title: Output roles
docs.text: role File sbom.cyclonedx _bom.json sbom.spdx _bom.spdx.json sbom.spdx3 _bom.spdx3.json vulnerabilities.trivy Trivy's own result. This is _security.json when nothing changed it, and _security_trivy.json (Trivy's result kept apart) when another engine added results or a finding was put under another id or moved to Advisories (see the security report) vulnerabilities.all _security.json, Trivy's result with the other engines' results merged in, and findings filed under a distribution advisory number reported under their CVE or in the top-level Advisories list vulnerabilities.other another engine's result (_security_grype.json, _security_cvebintool.json, _security_yocto.json) license-scan.scancode _scancode.json vendored.cyclonedx _vendored.cdx.json vex.reachability _reachability.cdx.json (--reachability) conformance _conformance.json input-description _input.json events bomlens-events.jsonl (BOMLENS_EVENTS=file) other any other file the run wrote (reports, sidecars)

docs.title: Package identifiers
docs.text:
Operating system packages in bom.json carry PURLs in the form Trivy and the purl-spec use, so they join the same packages from a Trivy scan or a supplier SBOM:

  • deb: the epoch is an epoch qualifier, not part of the version (pkg:deb/debian/bsdutils@2.38.1-5?arch=amd64&distro=debian-12&epoch=1).
  • apk: distro is the release id (distro=3.20.10).
  • deb, rpm, apk: no upstream qualifier; the source package is in the aquasecurity:trivy:SrcName property (with SrcVersion, SrcRelease, SrcEpoch), which is what Trivy matches distribution advisories on.
  • Qualifiers are sorted by name.

A change to this form is a major version change (see below).

docs.title: Image scans
docs.text:
In IMAGE mode syft reads the image first, and Trivy reads it again for the licenses of Debian packages (os-licenses), as does the file view. Those later reads take the image by the digest syft read, <repository>@sha256:..., so a tag that moves between the two reads cannot give them a different image. input.image records it:

"image": {
  "reference": "alpine:3.20",
  "source": "registry",
  "digest": "sha256:45e09956dc667c5eff3583c9d94830261fb1ca0be10a0a7db36266edf5de9e1d",
  "platform": "linux/arm64/v8",
  "index_digest": "sha256:d9e853e87e55526f6b2917df91a2115c36dd7c696a35be12163d44e6e2a4b6bc"
}
Field Meaning reference the image reference as given (TARGET_IMAGE) source where syft read it: registry (the registry: scheme, or a plain name with no Docker socket), daemon (docker: and podman:), archive (docker-archive:, oci-archive:, oci-dir:), other (containerd:), or null when the run stopped before syft read the image. With the socket, syft reads a plain name from the daemon and falls back to the registry when the daemon cannot give it the image, and its record does not name which it used. It is then told from the record: a Docker Hub repository digest written in full (index.docker.io/...) means registry, a listed tag means daemon, and anything else is unknown digest for registry, the manifest digest of the image read, one platform; for daemon and unknown, the repository digest recorded for that repository, which for a multi-platform image is the digest of its index and names the same content in the daemon and in the registry. null for an archive, which is read as it is, and when no digest could be resolved: a repository with no repository digest (an image built locally and never pushed), a name that is not a plain image name, or a syft source record that could not be written. The later reads then use the reference as given, and the log says so platform os/architecture[/variant] of the image read, or null. The variant is syft's architectureVariant, or else the variant in the image config (Docker writes v8 for arm64 images) index_digest registry only, present when the reference named an image index (manifest list) whose digest differs from digest

docs.title: Execution plan
docs.text:
A source scan runs in two containers: stage 1 resolves the dependencies in a cdxgen language image, stage 2 is this image in POSTPROCESS mode. A program that runs the containers itself (a Kubernetes Job, a hardened Docker runner) asks BomLens what to run with MODE=PLAN: mount the source read-only at /src and an output folder at /host-output, and the image writes bomlens-plan.json there and copies the files stage 1 mounts into bomlens-plan/. Nothing is scanned. The format is schemas/engine-plan-1.json.

docker run --rm -v "$PWD/src:/src:ro" -v "$PWD/out:/host-output" \
  -e MODE=PLAN -e PROJECT_NAME=app -e PROJECT_VERSION=1.0 -e HOST_OUTPUT_DIR=/host-output \
  -e BOMLENS_IMAGE_REF=ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens:<version> -e BOMLENS_IMAGE_DIGEST=sha256:... \
  ghcr.io/sktelecom/bomlens:<version>
Field Meaning status ok, or unsupported with reason and detail (android-sdk-image: the Android SDK image is built by you and not published) and no stages input.detected_ecosystem the language detection result that chose the stage 1 image output_file the SBOM file name stage 1 writes and stage 2 reads input_fingerprint what stage 1 reads, as sha256 values (see Input fingerprint); the same value as in the generate stage, and here also when there are no stages stages[] generate (stage 1) and postprocess (stage 2), in order

Each stage gives image and image_digest (stage 1 is always pinned by digest; stage 2 repeats BOMLENS_IMAGE_REF and BOMLENS_IMAGE_DIGEST), user, entrypoint, args, workdir, env (names and values to set), env_passthrough (names to pass from your own environment when set), network (whether it needs to reach the package registries) and mounts. A mount has a role (source, output, plan-file with a source path inside the output folder, the optional guard-state, an optional cache (cache-maven, cache-gradle), an optional settings file (maven-settings, maven-settings-security, gradle-properties, gradle-init-script, gradle-init-script-kts, gradle-init), or the optional trivy-db), a target and a mode. Mount a Trivy cache folder that holds a database (db/trivy.db) as trivy-db, read-only: with GENERATE_SECURITY=true (stage 2's report options are yours to set, as in the image reference), stage 2 then reads that database as it is, with no download, no update and no write, so it runs with no network and a read-only root. A trivy-db mount with no database fails scan-security with that reason; a database older than BOMLENS_TRIVY_DB_MAX_AGE_DAYS days (7, counted from UpdatedAt in db/metadata.json, when the database was built) records it as degraded (unavailable). Pass a value that fits how often you refresh the database. The source is writable in stage 1 only: the resolvers write lock files there, and stage 1 puts the tree back as it was when it finishes. A stage 1 that is killed (out of memory, a timeout) cannot; mount a folder of your own as guard-state and set BOMLENS_GUARD_ID to a unique id per scan, and after a kill run the same stage 1 again with BOMLENS_GUARD_RESTORE_ONLY=1 to restore the source. Pass HOST_UID and HOST_GID to both stages so the files they write belong to your user rather than root. Stage 2 also runs as any user (user is null, so you choose) with a read-only root filesystem, given a writable $TMPDIR (default /tmp, a tmpfs) and an output folder that user can write; a home it cannot write is replaced with a folder in $TMPDIR, unless something is mounted under it. Without a trivy-db mount Trivy downloads its database there, several hundred MB, which a memory-backed tmpfs counts as memory: mount trivy-db. Stage 1 runs as root: the resolvers install packages and write into the source. Stage 1's env also keeps the Go caches under /tmp/sbomhome (GOPATH=/tmp/sbomhome/go, GOMODCACHE=/tmp/sbomhome/go/pkg/mod, GOCACHE=/tmp/sbomhome/go-build), so go mod tidy runs with a read-only root filesystem and a writable /tmp, where the image's default /go/pkg cannot be created. A Go toolchain that go.mod asks for is downloaded into GOMODCACHE, which counts against a memory-backed /tmp. There is no Go cache mount role; mount a folder of your own at /tmp/sbomhome/go if you want the module cache kept between scans. cache-maven is a .m2-shaped folder (the Maven repository in repository/, and a settings.xml there is read when no maven-settings is mounted), and cache-gradle is a Gradle user home. Mount folders of the engine's own there, not a user's ~/.m2 or ~/.gradle: root-owned files there would break that user's own builds, and with HOST_UID and HOST_GID stage 1 hands what it wrote in these two mounts back to that user. Mount the user's settings files read-only under their own roles, which sit outside the cache folders, so no mount point is created inside them: Maven reads maven-settings and maven-settings-security in place of the cache's own, and the Gradle ones are copied into the Gradle user home before the first Gradle run and removed afterwards (a file the home already has is not replaced, and a copy that changed during the scan is kept). Scans that share one cache-gradle at the same time share the copies, and the last of them to end removes them; a scan that was killed leaves its copies for a day. Use the Gradle settings roles together with cache-gradle. The CLI mounts ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/bomlens/m2 and .../bomlens/gradle (%LOCALAPPDATA%\bomlens\cache on Windows) as the caches, and ~/.m2/settings.xml, ~/.m2/settings-security.xml, ~/.gradle/gradle.properties, ~/.gradle/init.gradle, ~/.gradle/init.gradle.kts and ~/.gradle/init.d read-only when they exist. It also runs with a read-only root filesystem given a writable /tmp, where HOME points (Gradle's files go there when the account's ~/.gradle cannot be written).

Stage 2's image is the one you name in BOMLENS_IMAGE_REF, whatever options you give stage 2. DEEP_CVE=true needs grype and DEEP_LICENSE=true needs scancode, which only the bomlens-deep-cve and bomlens-deep-license images have, so run stage 2 on that image and name it in BOMLENS_IMAGE_REF. Neither image has both tools: to have both, first remove an earlier <prefix>_scancode.json from the output folder, then run /usr/local/lib/sbom/deep-license.sh /src /host-output/<prefix>_scancode.json in the deep-license image (entrypoint bash, the same mounts, HOST_UID and HOST_GID so the file is yours), then stage 2 on the deep-cve image with DEEP_LICENSE=true and that script's exit code as BOMLENS_DEEP_LICENSE_RC, and optionally when it started and ended as BOMLENS_DEEP_LICENSE_STARTED and BOMLENS_DEEP_LICENSE_ENDED (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). When the output folder is inside the source tree, set DEEP_LICENSE_EXCLUDE to its folder name (folder names separated by spaces, left out at any depth) so the licence scan does not read the results. The script removes its output file when it does not finish (any exit code other than 0 or 6), and stage 2 keeps the file only for 0 and 6, removing it otherwise, and records the deep-license step from the code. The CLI does this with both options. On an image without the tool, the result manifest records the step (deep-cve or deep-license) as skipped (not_installed) and the run as succeeded_degraded. SECURITY_NVD_VERIFY=true with DEEP_CVE=true reads NVD_API_KEY in stage 2, which the plan lists in env_passthrough by name only.
